This note discusses the corrections and simplifications made to the AI-generated formalization, and records discrepancies found in the paper during the formalization. The Lean code is available at [URL].
tldr: A Lean 4 machine-checked formalization of the Dong-Yang classification of optimal (n,4) binary codes for binary symmetric channels, developed largely by AI and corrected by the authors.
motivation: To verify the correctness of Dong and Yang's classification of optimal finite-length binary block codes for BSCs and to document discrepancies found during formalization.
method: The authors fed the paper's proofs to an AI tool to generate a Lean 4 formalization, then verified the main theorem statements and accepted axioms, making corrections and simplifications.
result: They obtained a machine-checked proof of the classification, along with a record of corrections, simplifications, and discrepancies in the original paper.
conclusion: The work demonstrates AI-assisted formalization for classical coding theory, but it is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Eraser Enables Single-shot Quantum Holography With Undetected Photons
authors: Naru Yoneda, Nao Sakiyama, Luis Ordonez, Vishal Prajapati, Kanako Yoshimura, Osamu Matoba
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum holography with undetected photons (QHUP) enables the complex amplitude of infrared to be acquired beyond the sensitivity range of silicon based sensors, through induced coherence withoud induced emission. QHUP generally requires multiple phase-shifted holograms to retrieve the complex-amplitude distribution of an object, which limits measurement stability and temporal resolution. Although classical parallel phase-shifting holography provides a favorable balance between temporal and spatial resolution, it has not previously been implemented in QHUP because of the constraints imposed by photon distinguishability. In this study, we propose a quantum eraser-based geometric phase-shifting QHUP. By accurately erasing not only polarization distinguishability but also temporal distinguishability arising from differences in the optical paths, the complex-amplitude distribution of an object can be retrieved in a single shot using a silicon-based image sensor equipped with a polarization-filter array. This single-shot acquisition, combined with real-time processing, enables the observation of dynamic objects in the near-infrared spectral region. To the best of our knowledge, these experimental results constitute the first real-time acquisition of the complex-amplitude distribution of a near-infrared object using QHUP with a silicon-based image sensor equipped with a polarization-filter array. Furthermore, to enhance the reproducibility and applicability of this study, the experimental optical setup, bill of materials, and source code for real-time imaging have been made openly available. The ability to retrieve the complex-amplitude information carried by undetected photons in real time is expected to extend the applicability of QHUP to a wide range of fields, including spectroscopic imaging and semiconductor inspection.
tldr: A quantum-eraser-based geometric phase-shifting scheme enables single-shot quantum holography with undetected photons (QHUP), retrieving near-infrared complex-amplitude images in real time on a silicon sensor.
motivation: QHUP allows infrared imaging with silicon sensors via induced coherence, but usual implementations need multiple phase-shifted holograms, which harms stability and temporal resolution. Parallel phase-shifting had been impossible in QHUP due to photon distinguishability constraints.
method: The authors erase both polarization and temporal distinguishability using a quantum eraser with geometric phase shifting, combined with a polarization-filter-array silicon image sensor to capture the full complex amplitude in one shot, plus real-time processing and open-source hardware/software release.
result: They demonstrate single-shot, real-time acquisition of the complex-amplitude distribution of a moving near-infrared object, which they describe as the first such real-time QHUP imaging with a polarization-filter-array silicon sensor.
conclusion: The approach extends QHUP applicability to dynamic-object imaging, spectroscopic imaging, and semiconductor inspection, with full experimental reproducibility enabled by the released setup, bill of materials, and code.

title: Probabilistic Representation And Limit Theorems For Particle Numbers Of Quasi-free States
authors: Fanch Coudreuse, Simone Rademacher, Oliver Tse
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the particle number distribution of locally interacting bosonic quasi- free states, which arise in various areas of mathematical physics. We show that the particle number decomposes into an infinite sum of independent geometrically distributed random variables, confirming predictions from the physics literature. This representation yields exponential tail bounds for the particle number, a law of small numbers together with a large deviation principle at logarithmic speed when the lattice spacing diverges, and a central limit theorem when it vanishes. As an application, we obtain a detailed description of the statistics of the quantum depletion in Bose--Einstein condensates, with the constants explicit in terms of the scattering length of the interaction potential.
tldr: The paper provides a probabilistic representation and limit theorems for the particle number distribution of locally interacting bosonic quasi-free states.
motivation: Particle number statistics in bosonic quasi-free states are important in mathematical physics, particularly for understanding quantum depletion in Bose-Einstein condensates.
method: The authors decompose the particle number into an infinite sum of independent geometrically distributed random variables, then derive exponential tail bounds, a law of small numbers, a large deviation principle, and a central limit theorem under different lattice spacing limits.
result: They obtain explicit tail bounds, limit theorems, and a detailed description of the quantum depletion statistics in Bose-Einstein condensates with constants expressed in terms of the scattering length.
conclusion: The work rigorously confirms physics predictions and offers a probabilistic framework for particle number fluctuations in quasi-free bosonic systems, with applications to condensate depletion.

title: Consensus In Effective Model Inference For Disordered Ising Systems
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When independent learners are trained on data from the same disordered system, finite and noisy samples can lead them to different descriptions of the underlying physics. We quantify the reproducibility of such descriptions through consensus, the degree of agreement among independently trained models. In a teacher-student framework on the two-dimensional random-bond Ising model, an ensemble of students each infers a single uniform effective coupling from a finite set of equilibrium configurations drawn from one quenched bond realization. Aggregating the inferred couplings across students and realizations yields the consensus distribution, whose width quantifies the agreement among learners. The variance of this distribution separates exactly into a finite-sampling contribution, bounded below by inverse of Fisher information, and a quenched-disorder contribution. Sum of these two variance is minimized near critical region, so the consensus width has a minimum near the pseudocritical temperature that sharpens with increasing disorder. The two minima arise from different mechanisms: the sampling term inherits the critical peak of the Fisher information, while the disorder term is temperature-independent at leading order and acquires its critical minimum only at fourth order in the disorder strength, through the covariance between the linear and cubic responses to the bond disorder. Because the students fit a uniform coupling to a heterogeneous lattice, the inferred coupling also carries a misspecification bias that survives in the infinite-data limit. This bias displaces the minimum of the mean-squared error above the consensus minimum, so the temperature at which independent learners agree most closely is not the temperature at which their shared answer is most faithful.
tldr: This paper quantifies reproducibility of effective couplings inferred from finite samples of the two-dimensional random-bond Ising model via consensus among independently trained students.
motivation: Finite and noisy data can lead independent learners to different descriptions of the same disordered system, so the work aims to quantify agreement and separate sampling from quenched-disorder effects.
method: In a teacher-student framework, an ensemble of students each infers a single uniform effective coupling from finite equilibrium configurations drawn from one quenched bond realization, and the consensus distribution is analyzed via variance decomposition and Fisher information.
result: The consensus width is minimized near the pseudocritical temperature; its variance separates into a finite-sampling term bounded by inverse Fisher information and a quenched-disorder term, with the latter acquiring a critical minimum only at fourth order in disorder strength.
conclusion: Independent learners agree most closely near pseudocriticality, but a misspecification bias from fitting a uniform coupling to a heterogeneous lattice means this is not the temperature at which their shared effective answer is most faithful.

title: Henstock--Kurzweil Gauge Integral In The Non--Gaussian Regime: A Machine--Verified Construction
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a machine-checked construction of non-Gaussian functional integrals using the Henstock--Kurzweil gauge integral and Chernoff product approximations. The central object is a finite family of bosonic modes with action S(phi) = (1/2) phi^T A phi + lambda * sum_i phi_i^4, where A is positive definite. We prove that the one-mode integral I(omega, j, lambda) is finite, strictly positive, monotone and infinitely differentiable in the coupling lambda on [0, infinity). Its derivatives are given by convergent integrals of phi^{4k} with the same weight, not by the divergent perturbative series. The M-mode influence functional factorises into one-mode integrals and is bounded by its Gaussian value. A Chernoff / Lie--Trotter splitting handles the non-commutativity of the free and non-Gaussian generators. All statements are formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the accompanying file HkNonGaussian.lean is free of sorry and uses only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Four illustrative applications are worked out at the level of explicit formulas: the Duffing oscillator, local volatility (CEV) in finance, Wilson--Cowan neural fields, and non-Gaussian quantum reservoirs. The construction is completely direct and does not use Wick rotation, Wiener measure, zeta-regularisation or analytic continuation back from imaginary time.
tldr: The paper gives a machine-verified Lean 4 construction of non-Gaussian functional integrals using the Henstock–Kurzweil gauge integral and Chernoff product approximations.
motivation: Non-Gaussian functional integrals with quartic actions are central in quantum field theory and stochastic systems, but rigorous direct constructions avoiding Wick rotation and analytic continuation are challenging.
method: The authors define a one-mode integral for S(phi)=1/2 phi^T A phi + lambda sum phi_i^4, prove analytic properties, use a Chernoff/Lie–Trotter splitting for non-commuting generators, and formalise all results in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
result: They establish finiteness, strict positivity, monotonicity, infinite differentiability in lambda, derivative formulas via convergent integrals, factorisation of the M-mode influence functional, and a Gaussian upper bound, all free of sorry.
conclusion: The work provides a direct, machine-checked foundation for non-Gaussian functional integrals with illustrative applications to the Duffing oscillator, CEV finance, Wilson–Cowan neural fields, and non-Gaussian quantum reservoirs.

title: Generative Replay Mitigates Sample Starvation In Quantum Architecture Search
authors: Akash Kundu, Amit Kumar Jaiswal, Sebastian Feld, Prayag Tiwari
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can automate quantum architecture search, but its scalability is limited when useful circuit trajectories become rare in the rapidly expanding search space. Existing replay mechanisms reuse observed transitions; the proposed learned model produces additional predicted one step transitions from real state-action seeds. Here we introduce GenQAS, a tensor network-guided RL framework that combines a fixed matrix product state warm-start with prioritized generative replay. A learned local transition model generates synthetic circuit transitions on demand and mixes them with real experience during Double Deep Q-Network updates. Under a random exploration analysis, near ground state circuits occupy a rapidly shrinking region of the accessible state space. We investigate whether real data anchored synthetic replay can improve the effective training signal in this regime. Across chemical Hamiltonian benchmarks from 6 to 12 qubits, GenQAS improves fixed-budget success probability and identifies compact circuits at competitive energy error. At 12 qubits, it improves final success probability by up to [MATH] over passive replay. On a 15-qubit transverse field Ising model, GenQAS increases success probability from [MATH] to [MATH]. In a noisy 6-qubit BeH[MATH] transfer experiment, generative replay reduces the steps to chemical accuracy by [MATH]. These results show that generative replay can mitigate sample starvation in quantum architecture search and support more resource efficient circuit discovery.
tldr: GenQAS combines tensor-network (MPS) warm-starting with prioritized generative replay in a Double DQN framework to improve reinforcement-learning-based quantum architecture search under sample starvation.
motivation: RL-driven quantum architecture search struggles to scale because useful circuit trajectories become exceedingly rare as the search space grows, limiting the effective training signal available to the agent.
method: The authors build a fixed matrix-product-state warm start and train a learned local transition model that generates synthetic one-step circuit transitions on demand, mixing them with real experience during Double Deep Q-Network updates.
result: Across 6- to 12-qubit chemical Hamiltonian benchmarks GenQAS improves fixed-budget success probability (up to large gains over passive replay at 12 qubits), raises success probability on a 15-qubit transverse-field Ising model, and reduces steps to chemical accuracy in a noisy 6-qubit BeH2 transfer experiment.
conclusion: Generative replay anchored in real data mitigates sample starvation in quantum architecture search, enabling more resource-efficient circuit discovery.

title: Recent Advances On A Model For The Electromagnetic Dirac Field At Thermal Equilibrium
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review recent progress on a model for the relativistic electron-positron field interacting with a classical electromagnetic field at positive temperature. The ultimate goal is to advance our comprehension of how thermal backgrounds affect polarisation mechanisms of this quantum system.
tldr: This review discusses recent progress on a model of the relativistic electron-positron Dirac field interacting with a classical electromagnetic field at positive temperature.
motivation: The work aims to improve understanding of how thermal backgrounds influence polarization mechanisms in this quantum system.
method: It reviews and synthesizes recent developments in the theoretical modeling of the electromagnetic Dirac field at thermal equilibrium.
result: The abstract reports recent advances but does not specify concrete new results beyond the review scope.
conclusion: The paper seeks to advance comprehension of thermal effects on polarization in relativistic quantum systems, though it falls outside the user's prioritized research directions.

title: A Mathematical Theory Of Pragmatic Information
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a pragmatic information theory unifying communication, control, and decision-making. Its core is the isoteleia mapping, formalizing equifinality: distinct semantic paths leading to the same optimal action are pragmatically equivalent. This induces a three-tier hierarchy of syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic information, each abstraction discarding task-irrelevant distinctions. We develop pragmatic entropy, up/down mutual information, channel capacity, and rate-distortion, and prove three coding theorems generalizing Shannon's classical results. We introduce pragmatic value (VoI) and cost (CoI) of information as decision-theoretic duals to rate-distortion and capacity, respectively, and formulate a Lagrangian dual framework for cross-layer optimization. The pragmatic efficiency bound [MATH] quantifies the maximum net utility any resource-constrained intelligent system can extract, thereby establishing a fundamental behavioral capacity limit---generalizing Shannon's symbol-level capacity to goal-directed action. Extensions to continuous messages yield closed-form Gaussian expressions, while dynamic settings are addressed via a Bellman equation for sequential decision-making. This framework provides a rigorous foundation for task-oriented communication, networked control, autonomous systems, and embodied AI, shifting focus from symbol fidelity to the effectiveness of information in guiding actions, and offers a unified mathematical language for next-generation intelligent systems.
tldr: The paper proposes a pragmatic information theory that unifies communication, control, and decision-making through an isoteleia mapping and a three-tier hierarchy of syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic information.
motivation: To extend Shannon's classical information theory beyond symbol fidelity toward goal-directed action and task-oriented communication in intelligent systems.
method: It introduces pragmatic entropy, up/down mutual information, channel capacity, and rate-distortion, proves three coding theorems, and formulates value and cost of information with a Lagrangian dual framework.
result: The framework yields closed-form Gaussian expressions for continuous messages, a Bellman equation for sequential decisions, and a pragmatic efficiency bound on net utility for resource-constrained systems.
conclusion: It provides a mathematical foundation for task-oriented communication, networked control, and embodied AI, shifting focus from symbol fidelity to the effectiveness of information in guiding actions.

title: A General Proof Of The Fong-Tsui Conjecture
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a general proof of the Fong-Tsui conjecture for bounded operators on arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces. Specifically, we show that [MATH] implies that [MATH] is self-adjoint. The argument combines a positive inverse of a Sylvester map with a spectral cutoff determined by the norm of the positive defect [MATH]. A local vanishing lemma reduces the analysis to the classical squared self-adjointness criterion, while positivity of the defect yields a global norm contradiction. We formulate the argument as an abstract four-operator vanishing principle, without compactness, trace, or separability assumptions. We also establish a quantitative stability estimate: if [MATH] and [MATH], then [MATH]. The constant is independent of the dimension, and the exponent is not claimed to be optimal. Large language models (LLMs) were used to assist with proof development, algebraic calculations, numerical checks, and auditing of the arguments.
tldr: The paper proves the Fong-Tsui conjecture for bounded operators on arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces, showing that a certain operator condition implies self-adjointness, via a Sylvester-map positivity argument and a spectral cutoff.
motivation: The Fong-Tsui conjecture concerns an operator-theoretic characterization of self-adjointness under squared-commutator-type conditions, and had lacked a proof in the general bounded-operator setting without compactness, trace, or separability assumptions.
method: The proof combines a positive inverse of a Sylvester map with a spectral cutoff set by the norm of the positive defect, using a local vanishing lemma to reduce to the classical squared self-adjointness criterion plus a global norm contradiction, cast as an abstract four-operator vanishing principle; LLMs assisted with derivation and auditing.
result: The conjecture is proved in full generality, and a dimension-independent quantitative stability estimate is established for operators close to satisfying the hypotheses, with an exponent not claimed to be optimal.
conclusion: The work resolves a pure functional-analysis/operator-algebra question; while technically sophisticated, it has no apparent connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Narrow-line Magneto-optical Trap Of Titanium Atoms
authors: Rowan Duim, Scott Eustice, Jackson Schrott, Hiromitsu Sawaoka, Dan M. Stamper-Kurn
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We realize narrow-linewidth magneto-optical traps of [MATH]Ti, [MATH]Ti and [MATH]Ti atoms based on a 1040 nm-wavelength transition, cooling atoms to a minimum temperature in one dimension of [MATH] nK and a three-dimensional temperature of [MATH] [MATH]K. Atoms are pre-cooled in a broad-line magneto-optical trap and then transferred with about 25% efficiency to the narrow-line trap. We operate the narrow-line trap in two stages over 85 ms. First, a single cooling beam, blue-detuned from the narrow-linewidth atomic resonance, optically pumps and traps the atoms on a two-dimensional surface where the Zeeman shift from the applied spherical quadrupole magnetic field brings the light nearly to resonance. Second, four additional beams, counter-propagating in the transverse directions, cool and compress the atoms in all dimensions. The high magnetic moment of the laser cooling state makes the dynamics of the narrow-line titanium trap similar to those of other magnetic atoms. We measure the lifetime of the excited state of the transition to be [MATH] [MATH]s, indicating a transition linewidth of [MATH] kHz, and also measure isotope shifts on the narrow-line transition. We use Stern-Gerlach separation on the ultracold Ti gas to measure the [MATH]-distribution in the narrow-line magneto-optical trap, finding over 98% of the atoms in the stretched spin state.
tldr: Realization of narrow-linewidth magneto-optical traps for titanium isotopes, achieving nanokelvin temperatures and characterizing key atomic properties.
motivation: To extend laser cooling to titanium, a transition-metal atom with a narrow 1040 nm transition, which could enable new ultracold platforms for precision measurement and quantum simulation.
method: Atoms are pre-cooled in a broad-line MOT and transferred to a narrow-line MOT operated in two stages over 85 ms, followed by measurements of excited-state lifetime, isotope shifts, and spin distribution via Stern-Gerlach separation.
result: The trap achieves a minimum 1D temperature of nanokelvin scale and a 3D temperature of microkelvin scale, with about 25% transfer efficiency, a transition linewidth of kHz, and over 98% of atoms in the stretched spin state.
conclusion: Narrow-line titanium MOTs provide a new ultracold atomic platform whose dynamics resemble those of other magnetic atoms due to the high magnetic moment of the laser cooling state.

title: Universal Sampling Of Spin Systems Across Quenched Disorder
authors: Jing Liu, Yeyuan Wu, Ying Tang, Pan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Statistical physics extracts macroscopic laws by averaging over the many microscopic degrees of freedom of a system. Disordered systems demand a second and far harder average, one over the quenched randomness itself. The classic analytical routes, the replica and cavity methods, become uncontrolled outside mean-field or tree-like limits, and conventional numerical algorithms like parallel tempering require expensive, independent equilibration for every disorder realization. In this work, we introduce a universal neural variational framework that amortizes inference across the disorder ensemble, eliminating both the need for per-instance Markov chain equilibration and the cost of retraining instance-specific variational ansatzes. Built on an encoder-decoder Transformer architecture, after training once, it produces an explicit approximation to the Boltzmann distribution given previously unseen disorder realizations without further optimization. We validate this framework on 2D Edwards-Anderson models, and apply it to the random-bond Ising model, successfully capturing the Binder cumulant crossings near the Nishimori multicritical point. These results shift the object of variational inference from the single instance to the disorder ensemble, opening a route to frustrated many-body systems where instance-by-instance computation is prohibitive.
tldr: Introduces a universal neural variational framework that amortizes inference across quenched disorder realizations to sample classical spin systems without per-instance equilibration.
motivation: Disordered systems require averaging over quenched randomness, but traditional replica/cavity methods are uncontrolled beyond mean-field limits and parallel tempering needs expensive independent equilibration for each disorder realization.
method: Uses an encoder-decoder Transformer trained once to approximate the Boltzmann distribution for previously unseen disorder realizations, eliminating per-instance Markov chain equilibration and retraining.
result: Validated on 2D Edwards-Anderson models and applied to the random-bond Ising model, successfully capturing Binder cumulant crossings near the Nishimori multicritical point.
conclusion: Shifts variational inference from single-instance to disorder-ensemble learning, opening a route to frustrated many-body systems where instance-by-instance computation is prohibitive.

title: Fractional-order Hardware For Neuromorphic Computing: Is The Order Really The Problem?
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does a neuromorphic system need a true power-law memory kernel, and if so, can anyone build one? Neuromorphic systems process signals spanning many timescales at once, from milliseconds to tens of seconds. Integer-order circuits buy each additional timescale with an additional state variable. Fractional-order dynamics offer a different bargain: one operator whose power-law kernel carries a continuum of timescales, tuned by one parameter, the order alpha. A fractional derivative is non-local, so evaluating it costs storage and arithmetic that grow with the retained history, where an integer-order derivative costs a constant. This review organizes the hardware literature around that cost. We derive the retained history needed to hold the truncation error below a tolerance epsilon, show that it scales as epsilon^(-1/alpha), and set beside it a second and independent limit on the direct form: in fixed point the weights themselves underflow, so word length caps the usable history however long the buffer is. The two limits move at very different rates with the order, and where they cross decides whether a word length can serve an order at all. We use both to sort published hardware into three strategies, note a fourth the numerical literature has developed and this hardware has not, and survey digital, analog and device work. Along the way we ask whether the field is worried about the right obstacle. It is not. Fabricated constant-phase devices already span the orders two groups identify as task-optimal, so the order gap has largely closed, leaving a residual gap near 0.1 and at the lower order describing cortical adaptation. What remains is a frequency-band gap of about three decades at the low end. That corner is not empty, since double-layer electrodes work there, but every device in it is discrete, and no integrable thin-film element has been characterized there.
tldr: A review of fractional-order hardware for neuromorphic computing that argues the real bottleneck is not the achievable fractional order but a low-frequency band gap and the absence of an integrable thin-film constant-phase element.
motivation: Neuromorphic systems must process signals across many timescales, and fractional-order dynamics promise a continuum of timescales controlled by a single order parameter, but it is unclear whether fundamental order limits or practical hardware cost limits are the true obstacle.
method: The authors derive the retained history buffer needed to keep truncation error below a tolerance (scaling as epsilon^(-1/alpha)) and a second fixed-point underflow limit set by word length, then use these two limits to classify published digital, analog, and device-level hardware into three strategies, noting a fourth unexploited numerical approach.
result: The two limits cross at different rates with order, determining whether a given word length can support a given order; fabricated constant-phase devices already cover the task-optimal order range, leaving only a residual gap near order 0.1 and at the low order describing cortical adaptation.
conclusion: The field's perceived 'order problem' has largely closed, and the real remaining challenge is a roughly three-decade low-frequency band gap where only discrete double-layer electrodes exist and no integrable thin-film element has yet been characterized.

title: Consequences Of Matrices Sharing Eigenvalues And Eigenvectors
authors: Kayla Miller, Steven J. Miller, Fuzhen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While studying for a linear algebra final, the first named author prepared some test questions for herself to see how well she understood the material, and asked the second named author: We show how this excellent question is a great springboard to related questions, in particular when do equal eigenvalues and eigenvectors imply the matrices are, if not equal, at least closely related (such as similar or the transpose/complex conjugate transpose of each other)? The answer depends on how we interpret the question, and provides a great opportunity to talk about creating good questions. In particular, we characterize matrices [MATH] for which the transpose or conjugate transpose shares the same eigenvectors (regardless of eigenvalues) and, for each eigenvalue, the same eigenpair (equivalently, the same eigenspace). Thus, a square matrix [MATH] is Hermitian if and only if [MATH] has the same eigenpairs as [MATH]; moreover, if [MATH] is a real matrix with real eigenvalues and [MATH] has the same eigenvectors as [MATH], then [MATH] is symmetric.
tldr: A pedagogical linear algebra paper characterizing when matrices share eigenvalues and/or eigenvectors, and what that implies about similarity, transposition, or Hermiticity.
motivation: The question originated from a student's self-made exam problem about when equal eigenvalues and eigenvectors force matrices to be equal or closely related, and it grew into a broader discussion of how to ask good mathematical questions.
method: Elementary linear algebra arguments classifying matrices M whose transpose or conjugate transpose shares the same eigenvectors (and eigenspaces) as M, using spectral decomposition and symmetry arguments.
result: A square matrix is Hermitian if and only if it has the same eigenpairs as its conjugate transpose; similarly, a real matrix with real eigenvalues whose transpose shares its eigenvectors is symmetric.
conclusion: The paper offers clean characterizations linking eigenstructure coincidence to Hermiticity and symmetry, illustrating the value of well-posed questions in linear algebra pedagogy.

title: A Simple Complexity Lower Bound For Solving $Ax=b$
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we provide a short and direct proof that approximately solving [MATH] to relative error [MATH], where [MATH] has condition number [MATH] and unrestricted dimension, requires [MATH] matrix-vector multiplications in the worst case, even for randomized algorithms. This essentially recovers the lower bound of Derezi\'nski, Epperly and Meyer [2026] for this setting, whose elegant and more general approach inspired us to seek a short direct proof. A straightforward reduction implies the classical [MATH] lower bound for optimizing strongly convex quadratic functions, applicable to randomized algorithms.
tldr: A short direct proof that approximately solving Ax=b to relative error requires many matrix-vector multiplications in the worst case, even for randomized algorithms.
motivation: To recover the lower bound of Dereziński, Epperly and Meyer (2026) for this setting using a simpler, more direct argument.
method: Direct proof establishing a worst-case lower bound on the number of matrix-vector multiplications needed for approximate linear system solving, with a reduction to optimizing strongly convex quadratic functions.
result: The proof recovers the known lower bound and implies the classical lower bound for strongly convex quadratic optimization, applicable to randomized algorithms.
conclusion: A concise complexity-theoretic lower bound for linear algebra problems, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Carts: Contextual Autoregressive Rank Transcoding Steganography For Full-Capacity Keyed Text Encoding
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoregressive language models can be used to transform a payload text into a stegotext of identical token length by preserving per-position rank information across contexts - a methodology we formalize as Contextual Autoregressive Rank Transcoding Steganography (CARTS). While the Calgacus construction of Norelli et al. demonstrated this phenomenon experimentally, no formal security analysis existed. This paper provides the first rigorous treatment of CARTS. We show its exact correctness under deterministic model assumptions, introduce a rank-coordinate representation in which keys act as bijections on rank-vector space, define relevant security notions and the computational problems naturally associated with the construction - context search, key collisions, message equivocation, and non-commutativity of the encoding maps - and study the theoretical relationships between them, including the characterization of message equivocation in terms of context search, and the tension between key collisions and message equivocation. An empirical study on Llama 3 8B confirms exact recovery of the original payload in all tested cases, finds no key collisions under random key generation, establishes that a hand-crafted collision is local rather than global, and finds no commuting key pairs - suggesting resistance to the attack vectors studied. This work opens a formally grounded research agenda for the constructive use of language models in cryptography and privacy-preserving communication.
tldr: The paper formalizes Contextual Autoregressive Rank Transcoding Steganography (CARTS), a method for keyed text steganography using autoregressive language models, and provides correctness, security notions, and empirical tests on Llama 3 8B.
motivation: Existing steganographic constructions using language models, such as Calgacus, lacked formal security analysis despite experimental demonstrations, motivating a rigorous theoretical treatment.
method: The authors introduce a rank-coordinate representation where keys act as bijections on rank-vector space, define computational problems including context search, key collisions, and message equivocation, and test the construction empirically on Llama 3 8B.
result: The construction achieves exact payload recovery under deterministic model assumptions, random key generation yielded no collisions, hand-crafted collisions were local rather than global, and no commuting key pairs were found, suggesting resistance to studied attacks.
conclusion: The work opens a formally grounded research agenda for using language models constructively in cryptography and privacy-preserving communication, though it lies outside quantum information research interests.

title: Mms Allocation For Chores With Online Agent Arrivals
authors: Haolong Li, Zehan Lin, Huahua Miao, Xiaowei Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fair allocation of [MATH] indivisible chores to [MATH] agents with subadditive cost functions arriving online in an arbitrary order. Upon an agent's arrival, we are informed of her cost function and must irrevocably assign her a set of chores. We focus on the Maximin Share (MMS) fairness notion and aim to compute an allocation in which all items are assigned, and no agent incurs a cost more than [MATH] times her MMS. Without any prior information about the instance (other than [MATH] and [MATH]), we design an algorithm with a competitive ratio of [MATH] for any constant [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the number of cost function types. Our bound matches the best known offline approximation guarantees for MMS under subadditive costs and is nearly optimal with respect to all three parameters: we show that even for binary additive cost functions, no online algorithm can achieve a competitive ratio of [MATH]. We then consider the setting in which the [MATH] cost function types are known in advance (though the realized types of arriving agents are not). For additive cost functions, we provide an algorithm with a competitive ratio of [MATH], and show that constant-competitive algorithms do not exist for general [MATH], even for the binary additive setting. For binary additive functions when [MATH], we propose a [MATH]-competitive algorithm and establish a lower bound of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies online fair allocation of indivisible chores under Maximin Share (MMS) fairness when agents with subadditive cost functions arrive in arbitrary order and must be irrevocably assigned chores.
motivation: Fair division of chores is important in scheduling and resource allocation, yet most MMS results assume offline knowledge of all agents. This work addresses the online setting where agents arrive one by one and no prior distribution over cost functions is known.
method: The authors design online algorithms for MMS allocation with subadditive costs, parameterized by the number of cost function types, and prove matching or nearly matching lower bounds. They also consider a setting where the cost function types are known in advance but the realized types of arriving agents are not.
result: For general subadditive costs, they achieve a competitive ratio that matches the best offline approximation and is nearly optimal in all three parameters; they show that even for binary additive costs, no online algorithm can beat a certain bound. For additive costs with known types, they give a constant-competitive algorithm and prove that constant competitiveness is impossible for general MMS, with further refined bounds for binary additive costs.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive study of online MMS chore allocation, establishing tight or nearly tight competitive ratios and lower bounds that highlight fundamental limitations of online fairness.

title: The Computational Complexity Of Holant Problems On 4-regular Graphs From The Stable Subgroup Sequence Of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Holant framework provides a general setting for studying counting problems and includes graph homomorphisms (\#GH) and counting constraint satisfaction problems (\#CSP) as special cases. Over the past twenty years, a series of computational complexity dichotomies have been established for Holant problems, but the classification for complex-valued signatures is still open. The main obstacle is the case in which all signatures have even arity. In this paper, we establish a dichotomy for Holant problems with a complex-valued 4-ary signature, which is a key base case for the full classification of Holant problems. We present a new strategy by introducing Schur's theorem, the classification of finite subgroups of [MATH] and stable subgroup sequences into the proof. These new techniques are of independent interest.
tldr: This paper establishes a complexity dichotomy for Holant problems with a complex-valued 4-ary signature, using Schur's theorem and stable subgroup sequences from SL(2,C).
motivation: Holant problems generalize counting constraint satisfaction problems and graph homomorphisms, but classification for complex-valued signatures remains open, with even-arity signatures being a key obstacle.
method: The authors introduce Schur's theorem, the classification of finite subgroups of SL(2,C), and stable subgroup sequences into the complexity proof of Holant problems on 4-regular graphs.
result: They obtain a dichotomy for Holant problems with a complex-valued 4-ary signature, resolving a base case toward full classification of complex-valued Holant problems.
conclusion: The new algebraic techniques are of independent interest and may aid further complexity classifications, but the work is classical complexity theory with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems relevance.

title: New Method For Path-length Equalization Of Long Single-mode Fibers For Interferometry
authors: M. Anderson, J. D. Monnier, K. Ozdowy, J. Woillez, G. Perrin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability to use single mode (SM) fibers for beam transport in optical interferometry offers practical advantages over conventional long vacuum pipes. One challenge facing fiber transport is maintaining constant differential path length in an environment where environmental thermal variations can lead to cm-level variations from day to night. We have fabricated three composite cables of length 470 m, each containing 4 copper wires and 3 SM fibers that operate at the astronomical H band (1500-1800 nm). Multiple fibers allow us to test performance of a circular core fiber (SMF28), a panda-style polarization-maintaining (PM) fiber, and a lastly a specialty dispersion-compensated PM fiber. We will present experimental results using precision electrical resistance measurements of the of a composite cable beam transport system. We find that the application of 1200 W over a 470 m cable causes the optical path difference in air to change by 75 mm (+/- 2 mm) and the resistance to change from 5.36 to 5.50 {\Omega}. Additionally, we show control of the dispersion of 470 m of fiber in a single polarization using white light interference fringes ({\lambda}c=1575 nm, {\Delta}{\lambda}=75 nm) using our method.
tldr: The paper presents a method for equalizing and stabilizing the optical path length of long single-mode fibers used for beam transport in astronomical optical interferometry.
motivation: Fiber-based beam transport in interferometry is attractive over vacuum pipes but suffers from cm-level differential path-length drifts caused by day-night thermal variations.
method: Three 470 m composite cables containing copper wires and single-mode fibers (SMF28, panda PM, dispersion-compensated PM) were fabricated, and precision electrical resistance measurements of the copper wires were used as a proxy to monitor and equalize optical path-length changes.
result: Applying 1200 W over a 470 m cable changed the in-air optical path difference by 75 mm (±2 mm) and the resistance from 5.36 to 5.50 Ω; dispersion control over 470 m in a single polarization was demonstrated via white-light interference fringes.
conclusion: Electrical resistance measurements provide a practical handle for compensating thermal path-length drift in long single-mode fibers, enabling stable fiber transport for interferometric applications.

title: The Kinematic Structures And The Inertial Geometry Of A Moving Charge
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ask how much of the geometry a charged particle moves in is fixed by its motion, and how much a particle must bring. We ask of a symplectic structure only that it relate velocity to momentum as Hamilton's equations do, and we ask it of every energy at once. In particular, we show that the structures meeting that demand are the canonical one and its twists by a closed two-form of the base. A field provides the two-form, a particle the multiplier before it, which we identify constitutively with its charge. Thus, a single energy governs a family of structures, and each particle takes the one its charge fixes. We then ask what a particle must bring to be given a momentum, and we show that the degree of that map settles the degree at which a field enters Newton's Second Law. An antisymmetric bilinear form returns no Lorentz force, whilst a Randers metric returns one --- a length whose difference from a Riemannian one is linear in the velocity. Moreover, we find that metric already within the twisted structure, as its primitive over a level of the free energy, and its law of transport to be nonlinear, no affine connection being known to serve. Under an indefinite signature the length parts from the dynamics, and the extremals turn from shortest to longest. On the round sphere a monopole flux leaves no such metric, whilst the transport remains and prequantisation, given a unit of action, restricts the charge to a lattice. In this manner, we conclude that each charge-to-mass ratio receives a geometry of its own, so that by a functionalist criterion none of them is the spacetime of a charged particle.
tldr: The paper investigates the geometric structures required to describe a moving charged particle, linking symplectic forms, Randers metrics, and prequantization to charge-to-mass ratios.
motivation: The author asks how much of the geometry experienced by a charged particle is fixed by its motion and how much must be supplied by the particle itself, aiming to clarify the relationship between dynamics, field, and geometry.
method: The analysis uses symplectic geometry, closed two-forms, Finsler/Randers metrics, and prequantization to characterize the possible structures compatible with Hamilton's equations and Newton's second law.
result: It is shown that canonical symplectic structures twisted by a closed two-form provide the field, while a particle's charge fixes a multiplier; a Randers metric yields a Lorentz force and can be found as a primitive of the free energy, with indefinite signatures altering extremal behavior.
conclusion: Each charge-to-mass ratio receives its own geometry, so by a functionalist criterion no single geometry is the spacetime of a charged particle.

title: A New Generation Of Effective Core Potentials: Selected Heavy 5d And 6p Elements
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We expand the correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) library by developing semi-local pseudopotentials and matching basis sets by heavy-elements from [MATH] (Hf, Os, Hg) and [MATH] (Tl, Po, At, Rn) blocks. In order to accurately capture scalar relativistic effects, spin-orbit coupling, and electron-electron correlation, we implement a tiered core-valence partitioning strategy across three distinct resolutions. This includes a small 60-core (Hf, Os, Hg) that explicitly correlates subvalence shells, a large 78-core definition for the main-group elements that rigorously accounts for core polarization and relaxation effects in sparse valence environments, and an intermediate 68-core partition for Hg and Tl. This 68-core architecture represents a unique development in the ccECP library, optimizing the balance between accuracy and computational efficiency in a manner unexplored for ligther elements. Optimized against relativistic all-electron CCSD(T) references, the ccECPs deliver outstanding atomic precision, achieving a global average atomic low-lying states deviation of just 0.045 eV. This accuracy translates directly to robust molecular transferability, systematically restricting dissociation energy discrepancies to under 0.03 eV, equilibrium bond lengths to within 0.005 {\AA}. By enforcing a regularized, finite potential at the origin for enhanced numerical stability in stochastic quantum Monte Carlo methods, this library removes a critical methodological bottleneck for predictive many-body simulations of heavy-element systems and materials.
tldr: The paper develops new correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) and matching basis sets for heavy 5d and 6p elements to enable accurate relativistic many-body simulations.
motivation: Heavy-element systems require pseudopotentials that accurately capture scalar relativistic effects, spin-orbit coupling, and electron correlation, but existing libraries lack optimized partitions for these elements.
method: The authors construct semi-local pseudopotentials with a tiered core-valence partitioning strategy (60-core, 68-core, 78-core) and optimize them against relativistic all-electron CCSD(T) reference data, with a regularized finite potential at the origin for quantum Monte Carlo stability.
result: The ccECPs achieve a global average atomic low-lying state deviation of 0.045 eV, with molecular dissociation energy discrepancies under 0.03 eV and equilibrium bond lengths within 0.005 Å.
conclusion: The expanded ccECP library removes a methodological bottleneck for predictive many-body simulations of heavy-element systems and materials.

title: Spectral And Numerical Radius Preservers On Pairs Of Unitarily Similar Operators
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a complex Hilbert space. We characterize the bijective linear maps [MATH] that preserve the spectral radius, respectively the numerical radius, on pairs of unitarily similar operators. We also characterize bijective linear maps that transform unitary similarity into similarity. Our results cover both finite and infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, with no separability assumption in the latter case.
tldr: The paper characterizes bijective linear maps that preserve the spectral radius or numerical radius on pairs of unitarily similar operators, and maps that turn unitary similarity into similarity, on finite- and infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
motivation: Linear preserver problems seek to classify transformations that leave spectral invariants unchanged; extending this to pairs of unitarily similar operators addresses a natural operator-theoretic question.
method: The author uses techniques from functional analysis and operator theory to classify bijective linear preservers of spectral and numerical radii on such pairs, without assuming separability in infinite dimensions.
result: Complete characterizations are obtained for the relevant preservers and for bijective linear maps transforming unitary similarity into similarity, covering both finite and infinite-dimensional settings.
conclusion: The work is a contribution to pure operator theory and linear preserver problems, with no direct relevance to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Diagrammatic Categorification Of Verma Modules I: Braiding
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the extensions of KLRW algebras to tensor products of Verma module representations of [MATH]. Our motivation is to construct a theory of Khovanov homology for knot complements in [MATH] (and which also categorifies the Gukov-Manolescu two-variable series for knot complements), which will be done in the second part of this work. We construct the categorification of R-matrices for Verma modules as functors given by derived tensor products with diagrammatic bimodules and explicitly compute their projective resolutions. We also prove these braiding functors induce an action of the braid group on the relevant categories. Then, we describe how to incorporate strands in finite-dimensional representations of [MATH], thereby establishing functors that serve as the Khovanov homology on a braid complement. In the case of the unknot, this gives knot homologies in [MATH], which we compare to Annular Khovanov Homology through several examples and show they are very closely related, conjecturing they are of the same dimension. We conclude with a proposal for the categorification of the cups and caps of Verma module colored strands, which we build upon in the next paper.
tldr: This paper develops a diagrammatic categorification of Verma modules via KLRW algebras, constructing braiding functors and relating them to Khovanov homology for knot complements.
motivation: The work is motivated by constructing Khovanov homology for knot complements and categorifying the Gukov-Manolescu two-variable series.
method: The authors extend KLRW algebras to tensor products of Verma module representations, construct categorified R-matrices as derived tensor products with diagrammatic bimodules, and compute projective resolutions.
result: They prove the braiding functors induce a braid group action and establish functors corresponding to Khovanov homology on braid complements, with examples connecting to Annular Khovanov Homology.
conclusion: The paper proposes a framework for categorifying cups and caps of Verma module colored strands, to be built upon in subsequent work.

title: Full-window Branch Discovery And Loss-selected EnKF Continuation For Data Assimilation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a framework for offline full-window branch discovery, optionally followed by online continuation with an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF). Three mechanisms drive the branch search: adjoint path-kernel (APK) differentiation balances kernel differentiation and correction-stabilized path perturbation, shifting the optimization from exploration to exploitation; an optimized Gaussian initial law broadens the search over initial-state basins; and loss-weighted mixing across independent runs recombines successful path components. We may then select an interior state using a local loss and continue online with an EnKF. In 40-dimensional Lorenz-96 experiments, the mean offline path RMSE of APK is 4.3 times smaller than that of population weak-[MATH]. The resulting APK-EnKF method has a mean online RMSE 64 times smaller than that of ordinary EnKF.
tldr: The paper introduces an adjoint path-kernel (APK) framework for offline full-window branch discovery, combined with an ensemble Kalman filter for online continuation, achieving large RMSE reductions in Lorenz-96 data assimilation experiments.
motivation: Data assimilation requires accurate identification of system trajectories over a time window, but standard methods struggle to efficiently search multiple initial-state basins and to transition from offline state estimation to online filtering.
method: Three mechanisms drive the branch search: adjoint path-kernel differentiation balancing kernel differentiation with correction-stabilized path perturbation, an optimized Gaussian initial law broadening the search over initial-state basins, and loss-weighted mixing across independent runs; an interior state is then selected via local loss and continued online with an EnKF.
result: In 40-dimensional Lorenz-96 experiments, APK achieves a mean offline path RMSE 4.3 times smaller than population weak-constraint methods, and the APK-EnKF method yields a mean online RMSE 64 times smaller than ordinary EnKF.
conclusion: Combining branch discovery with loss-selected initialization substantially improves filter performance, suggesting a practical route to more accurate offline-to-online data assimilation for chaotic dynamical systems.

title: A Scale Invariance Property Of Pca
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The PCA algorithm is sensitive to changes in measurement scale. Measuring one variable of a system in inches rather than centimeters, say, alters both its principal axes and principal eigenvalues. Although this scale dependence is generally complicated, we show here that it nevertheless obeys a strict invariance property: under a continuous scale adjustment, the initial state's [MATH]-th largest principal component (ordered by eigenvalue) continuously evolves into the final state's [MATH]-th largest principal component, for each [MATH]. In this sense, we can say that the modes of PCA are "order-stable" with respect to changes in measurement scale. A special case occurs when scaling along directions that are orthogonal to some modes. Here, apparent eigenvalue crossings can occur. However, we show that we can interpret these apparent crossings as cases where the modes instantaneously swap their orientation, in this way maintaining the required order stability.
tldr: The paper proves an order-stability property of principal component analysis under continuous changes of measurement scale.
motivation: PCA is known to depend on measurement units, which complicates interpretation when variables are rescaled. The author seeks a structural invariance that survives arbitrary scale adjustments.
method: The work analyzes how principal axes and eigenvalues evolve under a continuous scaling of variables, tracking the ordered principal components and treating apparent eigenvalue crossings as instantaneous orientation swaps.
result: It is shown that under any continuous scale adjustment, the initial state's k-th largest principal component continuously evolves into the final state's k-th largest principal component, preserving order stability.
conclusion: PCA modes are order-stable with respect to measurement scale changes, offering a precise invariance interpretation even when eigenvalue crossings appear.

title: HermiCache: Enclave-Aware Cache Replacement For Trusted Execution Environments
authors: Oussama Elmnaouri, Pascal Cotret, Vianney Lap\^otre, Lo\"ic Lagadec
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) protect enclave memory from untrusted software but remain vulnerable to cache-based side-channel attacks due to shared microarchitectural resources. Existing countermeasures use techniques such as cache partitioning or randomization: these solutions are not ideal if a designer wants fine-grained configurations and a deterministic protection. In this paper, we introduce HermiCache which is an answer to these requirements. HermiCache is designed for RISC-V cores and has been implemented in the OpenHwGroup CVA6 core with a Keystone TEE for the software layer. The solution has an area overhead of 6% on the processor core.
tldr: HermiCache is an enclave-aware cache replacement policy for RISC-V cores that mitigates cache-based side-channel attacks against Trusted Execution Environments.
motivation: TEEs protect enclave memory from untrusted software but remain vulnerable to cache-timing side channels because the cache is a shared microarchitectural resource; existing partitioning or randomization countermeasures lack fine-grained configuration and deterministic protection.
method: The authors design HermiCache, a cache replacement scheme integrated into the OpenHW Group CVA6 RISC-V core with a Keystone TEE software layer, providing deterministic, configurable protection.
result: The implementation incurs only about 6% area overhead on the processor core while providing the targeted side-channel protection.
conclusion: Deterministic enclave-aware cache replacement offers a practical, low-overhead alternative to partitioning or randomization for securing TEEs on RISC-V cores.

title: Beyond Static Guarantees: Measuring The Static-Pass Dynamic-Fail Gap In Security-Sensitive And LLM-Generated Python Code
authors: Jessica Pourleyli, Maitreyee Das Urmi, Glaucia Melo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) fuel the quest for scalable methods to assess the security of generated and security-sensitive software. Static analysis is widely adopted as a scalable, reproducible, and inexpensive security gate, but cannot directly observe runtime exploit behaviour. Vulnerabilities dependent on adversarial inputs, execution context, or exploit chaining may evade static checks while remaining exploitable in practice, yet passing static analysis is often treated as evidence of secure behaviour. This paper introduces the Static-Pass Dynamic-Fail (SPDF) phenomenon and a three-stage agentic pipeline combining static scanning, LLM-driven Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) reasoning, and autonomous exploit verification in isolated Docker containers. We evaluate 1,355 Python samples from SecurityEval, RedCode, and CyberNative datasets. Of the 654 samples producing no findings under the composite Bandit-Semgrep gate, the LLM detection stage identified 394 candidate vulnerabilities across 235 files. Dynamic verification confirmed or partially confirmed exploitability in 95 files, yielding an inclusive pipeline rate of 14.53% (roughly 1 in 7 statically clean samples). This rate represents the proportion of Bandit-Semgrep-clean samples for which the pipeline identified a candidate vulnerability and obtained runtime evidence supporting exploitability. Outcomes varied by dataset: among candidate file--CWE pairs, confirmed exploitability was 33.7% for RedCode, 28.6% for CyberNative, and 5.4% for SecurityEval. Several frequently confirmed classes, including CWE-338 and CWE-916, were flagged by neither Bandit nor Semgrep. These findings indicate that static-analysis success and runtime security are hierarchical layers of software assurance rather than interchangeable measures, and have the potential to reshape how AI-generated and security-sensitive code is evaluated.
tldr: The paper introduces the Static-Pass Dynamic-Fail (SPDF) phenomenon and an agentic pipeline (static scanning + LLM CWE reasoning + Docker-based exploit verification) to quantify vulnerabilities that evade static analysis in security-sensitive and LLM-generated Python code.
motivation: Static analysis is widely used as a cheap, scalable security gate, but passing static checks is often wrongly treated as evidence of runtime security; the authors aim to measure the gap between static cleanliness and actual exploitability.
method: They evaluate 1,355 Python samples from SecurityEval, RedCode, and CyberNative using a three-stage pipeline: composite Bandit-Semgrep scanning, LLM-driven CWE reasoning, and autonomous exploit verification in isolated Docker containers.
result: Of 654 Bandit-Semgrep-clean samples, the LLM stage flagged 394 candidate vulnerabilities in 235 files, and dynamic verification confirmed exploitability in 95 files (14.53% inclusive pipeline rate), with per-dataset confirmation rates of 33.7% (RedCode), 28.6% (CyberNative), and 5.4% (SecurityEval); several frequently confirmed CWEs (e.g., CWE-338, CWE-916) were missed by both static tools.
conclusion: Static-analysis success and runtime security should be viewed as hierarchical layers of software assurance rather than interchangeable measures, which has implications for how AI-generated and security-sensitive code is evaluated.

title: Pearl: A Task-Aware Framework For Evaluating Differentially Private Synthetic Educational Data
authors: Xianghui Meng, Yujing Zhang, Jionghao Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personalized learning systems rely on real learner data, including performance, behavior, and demographic information, but these data are highly privacy-sensitive. Differentially private (DP) synthetic data can support system development and educational research while reducing exposure of individual learners. Existing evaluations, however, assess privacy and predictive usefulness separately, without determining whether synthetic learner data remain usable for the intended personalized learning task. We introduce PEARL (Privacy-Equivalence Audit and Release Ledger), which approves a DP synthetic educational dataset only when it passes all required checks of validity, privacy protection, predictive usefulness, and suitability for the intended educational task, while recording why each rejected dataset fails. Across 96 study settings, each defined by a dataset, data-generation method, privacy budget, and random seed, only 12 produced synthetic datasets that passed all applicable PEARL checks. Many privacy-protected datasets were rejected for omitting important outcome groups, such as withdrawn students, or for failing to preserve the order of learning activities. Fairness analysis further showed that some datasets passing privacy and predictive-usefulness checks still yielded unequal at-risk prediction performance across groups defined by disability and socioeconomic background. Moreover, Deep Knowledge Tracing and Self-Attentive Knowledge Tracing learned no meaningful next-response patterns from any tested synthetic knowledge-tracing dataset, showing that privacy protection alone does not guarantee usefulness for dropout prediction, knowledge tracing, or adaptive tutoring.
tldr: PEARL is a task-aware auditing framework that approves differentially private synthetic educational datasets only when they satisfy validity, privacy, predictive-usefulness, and task-suitability checks.
motivation: Personalized learning systems need sensitive learner data, and while DP synthetic data can reduce privacy exposure, existing evaluations judge privacy and usefulness separately and never verify whether the synthetic data still supports the intended educational task.
method: The authors propose PEARL (Privacy-Equivalence Audit and Release Ledger), which runs a battery of validity, privacy, predictive-usefulness, and task-suitability checks, accepting a dataset only if all applicable checks pass and logging the rejection reasons, evaluated across 96 study settings spanning datasets, generation methods, privacy budgets, and seeds.
result: Only 12 of 96 settings produced acceptable synthetic datasets; many were rejected for omitting outcome groups such as withdrawn students or failing to preserve learning-activity order, and some accepted datasets showed unequal at-risk prediction performance by disability and socioeconomic background, while Deep Knowledge Tracing and Self-Attentive Knowledge Tracing learned no meaningful patterns from any synthetic knowledge-tracing dataset.
conclusion: Privacy protection alone does not guarantee usefulness, and DP synthetic educational data must be audited against the specific downstream learning task to be safely and fairly released.

title: A Nonrecursive Method For Computing The Off-diagonal Small-time Heat Kernel Expansion
authors: Alexey V. Reznichenko Vyacheslav O. Guba
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a nonrecursive method to compute the small-time heat kernel asymptotic expansion. The Klein-Gordon operator in flat space-time coupled to electromagnetic fields is considered. We obtain closed-form expressions for the expansion coefficients up to the second order in time. Our approach can be regarded as an extension of the method described in [R.I. Nepomechie, Phys. Rev. D 31, 3291 (1985)], but unlike that work, our approach is valid for arbitrary space-time dependence of the heat kernel, i.e. for off-diagonal values. We verify that our results correctly reproduce small-time asymptotics of the heat kernel for a plane wave field and for constant electromagnetic fields.
tldr: A nonrecursive method is presented for computing the off-diagonal small-time heat kernel expansion for a Klein-Gordon operator coupled to electromagnetic fields.
motivation: Existing recursive methods for heat kernel expansions are limited to diagonal cases, while off-diagonal expansions are needed for more general space-time dependent problems.
method: The authors extend a known recursive approach to arbitrary space-time dependence, deriving closed-form expressions for expansion coefficients up to second order in time.
result: Closed-form expressions for the off-diagonal heat kernel coefficients up to second order are obtained and verified for plane wave and constant electromagnetic fields.
conclusion: The nonrecursive method generalizes previous work and provides a practical tool for computing off-diagonal heat kernel asymptotics in quantum field theory contexts.

title: A Note On The Browder S-spectrum Of A Bounded Quaternionic Operator
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a bounded operator on a separable right quaternionic Hilbert space and let [MATH] be the set of compact operators commuting with [MATH]. We establish the formula \[ \sigb(A)=\bigcap_{K\in\CA} \sS(A+K), \] a quaternionic analogue of the classical characterization of the complex Browder spectrum. The proof rests on a factorization lemma (Lemma~), a consequence of the Riesz--Schauder theorem and an ascent/descent argument, and on the characterization [MATH] in terms of S-eigenvalues of finite type, due to Arzini and Jaatit , for which we give here an independent proof (Lemma~). We also record two consequences of independent interest: the intersection defining [MATH] may be restricted, without loss, to operators commuting with [MATH] (Corollary~); and, by a separate argument resting on the ascent/descent stability results of , the stronger pointwise statement [MATH] holds for a fixed [MATH] and arbitrary [MATH] (Theorem~), known in the complex case.
tldr: The paper proves a quaternionic analogue of the Browder spectrum characterization for bounded operators on a separable right quaternionic Hilbert space.
motivation: The classical characterization of the complex Browder spectrum is extended to the quaternionic setting, motivated by the need for spectral theory of quaternionic operators.
method: The proof uses a factorization lemma derived from the Riesz-Schauder theorem, an ascent/descent argument, and a characterization of the Browder S-spectrum via finite-type S-eigenvalues.
result: It establishes that the Browder S-spectrum equals the intersection of the S-spectra of A+K over all compact operators K commuting with A, with additional corollaries and a pointwise stronger statement.
conclusion: The work contributes to quaternionic operator theory and spectral analysis, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Decrease In Sectional Curvature Of The Fisher--Rao Manifold Of Beta Distributions
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the paper, the author develops a general convexity lemma and applies it to demonstrate the monotonic decrease of a function involving polygamma functions, arising from the sectional curvature of the Fisher--Rao manifold of beta distributions.
tldr: The paper proves that a function involving polygamma functions and arising from the sectional curvature of the Fisher--Rao manifold of beta distributions decreases monotonically, using a general convexity lemma.
motivation: Understanding curvature properties of statistical manifolds such as the Fisher--Rao manifold of beta distributions is of interest in information geometry, and proving monotonicity of related special functions can simplify curvature analysis.
method: The author develops a general convexity lemma and applies it to a function involving polygamma functions that appears in the sectional curvature formula.
result: The lemma implies the monotonic decrease of the targeted polygamma-function expression, thereby establishing the claimed curvature monotonicity.
conclusion: This is a mathematical contribution to the information geometry of beta distributions, with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A New Uncertainty Principle At Low Energies
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new method to prove uncertainty principles for functions of low energy in a very general set-up. This leads to results for metric measure spaces, Dirichlet spaces and graphs under rather weak assumptions.
tldr: The paper presents a new method to prove uncertainty principles for low-energy functions in general settings including metric measure spaces, Dirichlet spaces, and graphs.
motivation: Uncertainty principles are fundamental in analysis, but existing results often rely on strong assumptions or specific domains, limiting their applicability.
method: The authors develop a general framework that yields uncertainty principles under weak assumptions for functions of low energy on metric measure spaces, Dirichlet spaces, and graphs.
result: They obtain new uncertainty principle results in these broad settings, demonstrating the method's flexibility and generality.
conclusion: The work provides a versatile tool for proving low-energy uncertainty principles with potential applications across mathematical analysis and spectral theory.

title: Structural Consequences Of The Schur $p$-property For Lipschitz-free $p$-spaces
authors: Fernando Albiac, Jos\'e L. Ansorena, Marek C\'uth
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] in the light of the Schur [MATH]-property and the compact reduction, J. Geom. Anal. 36 (2026), Paper No. 54] on the Schur [MATH]-property, together with several related problems. They also confirm a prediction of Kalton and the first-named author from 2009: no infinite-dimensional [MATH]-Banach space has the [MATH]-Lipschitz lifting property. Further applications reveal a sharp contrast between the linear and Lipschitz structures of nonlocally convex spaces.
tldr: The paper studies structural consequences of the Schur p-property for Lipschitz-free p-spaces, establishing results on compact reduction and the p-Lipschitz lifting property in nonlocally convex Banach spaces.
motivation: The authors aim to extend and apply recent work on the Schur p-property and related problems, including a 2009 prediction about infinite-dimensional p-Banach spaces.
method: The work uses functional analytic techniques from Banach space theory, including Schur p-property, compact reduction, and Lipschitz-free p-space constructions.
result: They confirm that no infinite-dimensional p-Banach space has the p-Lipschitz lifting property and reveal sharp contrasts between linear and Lipschitz structures of nonlocally convex spaces.
conclusion: The findings advance the structural theory of Lipschitz-free p-spaces and clarify limitations imposed by the Schur p-property.

title: Symplecto-rigidity And Bootstrap For Anosov Symplectomorphisms And Contact Anosov Flows
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a sequel to the authors' paper on rigidity of higher dimensional contact Anosov flows~[GRH]. At the time the authors were unaware of much earlier work of Hamenst\"adt~[Ham] devoted to the same problem. The methods of~[GRH] and~[Ham] are overlapping but not entirely the same. In this paper we strengthen some the results of Hamenst\"adt, by further bootstrapping the regularity of the conjugacy of 2-pinched contact Anosov flows. We also introduce a notion of symplecto-rigidity for symplectomorphisms and prove that some Anosov diffeomorphisms are symplecto-rigid. We further combine symplecto-rigidity with various rigidity techniques to establish a number of smooth rigidity results of Anosov symplectomorphisms. Some new phenomena are present in the realm of Anosov symplectomorphism. For example, while the well-known de la Llave example on the 4-torus demonstrates absence of rigidity in the space of smooth Anosov diffeomorphisms, however, we prove that it is rigid in the space of Anosov sympelctomorphisms.
tldr: This paper studies rigidity phenomena for Anosov symplectomorphisms and contact Anosov flows, introducing a notion of symplecto-rigidity and bootstrapping regularity of conjugacies.
motivation: The authors aim to strengthen earlier rigidity results of Hamenstadt for 2-pinched contact Anosov flows and to develop new rigidity machinery for symplectomorphisms, motivated by the contrast between smooth Anosov diffeomorphism rigidity and the special structure of symplectic settings.
method: The approach combines bootstrapping techniques for the regularity of conjugacies of contact Anosov flows with a newly introduced notion of symplecto-rigidity, fused with existing smooth rigidity techniques for hyperbolic dynamics.
result: They show that certain Anosov diffeomorphisms are symplecto-rigid, and notably prove that the de la Llave example on the 4-torus, which lacks rigidity among smooth Anosov diffeomorphisms, is rigid within the space of Anosov symplectomorphisms.
conclusion: The work reveals new rigidity phenomena specific to Anosov symplectomorphisms and strengthens prior results on contact Anosov flows, highlighting symplectic structure as a source of additional constraints.

title: Preserving Structure In Variational Data Assimilation Of Hyperbolic Conservation Laws Via Regularization
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperbolic conservation laws pose a challenging setting for variational data assimilation, since the Gaussian assumption imposes a smoothness that smears jump discontinuities. A sparsity promoting regularization can help to mitigate this problem by incorporating a structural prior into the variational objective. Care must be taken when choosing this prior because it serves to counterbalance both a structurally misspecified background-error covariance, which introduces spurious oscillations over smooth regions, as well as spatially sparse observations, which leave too little data to constrain the state. Moreover, state variables of hyperbolic conservation laws typically do not have piecewise constant structure, which is an assumption made when using standard sparsity-promoting operators, such as total variation. Indeed the underlying {\em variability} of hyperbolic conservation law solutions are neither known in advance nor fixed. Hence using higher order total variation is also not suitable. Here we introduce a new regularization term for data assimilation, built on the sparsity promoting residual transform that neither commits to a fixed smoothness order nor requires the underlying variability to be known a priori. We solve the resulting nonconvex objective within a three-dimensional variational framework using generalized sparse Bayesian learning. This approach replaces a global \(\ell _{1}\) penalty with a hierarchical conditional Gaussian prior on the residual transform, where a learned hyper-prior yields location-specific weights attached to each spatial point. Numerical experiments across scalar, shallow-water, and Euler test problems show that this regularization term resolves discontinuities more accurately than total variation, and that its advantage grows as the background-error covariance becomes misspecified and the observations become sparser.
