tldr: A new regularization method for variational data assimilation of hyperbolic conservation laws that avoids fixed smoothness assumptions by using a sparsity-promoting residual transform with learned location-specific weights.
motivation: Standard variational data assimilation struggles with discontinuous solutions of hyperbolic conservation laws because Gaussian assumptions smear jumps, and total variation regularization assumes piecewise constant structure that is often invalid.
method: The authors introduce a regularization term based on a sparsity-promoting residual transform and solve a nonconvex objective via generalized sparse Bayesian learning within a 3D-Var framework, using a hierarchical conditional Gaussian prior to learn location-specific weights.
result: Numerical experiments on scalar, shallow-water, and Euler problems show that the proposed regularization resolves discontinuities more accurately than total variation, with growing advantage as background-error covariance misspecification and observation sparsity increase.
conclusion: The residual-transform-based regularization offers a flexible approach for preserving structure in data assimilation of hyperbolic conservation laws without committing to a fixed smoothness order or known variability.

title: Admissible Fourier Lengths, Kam Reducibility, And Spectral Applications
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a perturbative KAM reducibility theory for one-frequency [MATH] cocycles based on an admissible Fourier length [MATH]. The regularity relevant to the iteration is measured by positive adapted Fourier width rather than ordinary smoothness in the Euclidean length [MATH]. The same length governs Fourier decay, truncation and resonance scales, and the arithmetic condition controlling the small divisors. This framework contains the classical analytic and Gevrey settings, while non-monotone choices of [MATH] allow classical nowhere differentiable Weierstrass-type perturbations and continuous perturbations outside every positive H\"older class. As spectral applications, we obtain purely absolutely continuous spectrum for every phase and [MATH]-H\"older continuity of the integrated density of states for the associated quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. The Aubry dual has pure point spectrum for Lebesgue almost every dual phase, with eigenfunctions exponentially localized in the metric induced by [MATH]. We also construct nowhere differentiable quasiperiodic potentials with purely absolutely continuous Cantor spectrum.
tldr: The paper develops a perturbative KAM reducibility theory for one-frequency cocycles using an admissible Fourier length, with applications to quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators.
motivation: The work aims to extend classical analytic and Gevrey KAM reducibility frameworks to more general regularity classes, including non-monotone Fourier lengths and nowhere differentiable perturbations.
method: It measures regularity via positive adapted Fourier width rather than ordinary smoothness, and uses this length to control Fourier decay, truncation, resonance scales, and small divisor arithmetic conditions.
result: The theory yields purely absolutely continuous spectrum for every phase and Hölder continuity of the integrated density of states, while the Aubry dual has pure point spectrum with exponentially localized eigenfunctions for almost every dual phase.
conclusion: The framework unifies and extends existing reducibility results and constructs nowhere differentiable quasiperiodic potentials with purely absolutely continuous Cantor spectrum.

title: Optimal Networks With Accumulative Costs And Bidirectional Communication
authors: Fernando Tohm\'e Juan M. C. Larrosa
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is an extension of the approach of Larrosa and Tohm\'e (2003), in which the payoff function is modified by allowing information to flow in both directions. Costs continue to be paid by the agent who initiates the connection, so this asymmetry reveals changes in the final equilibrium topology. We find that several optimal topologies persist as Nash networks, but that a strict Nash network corresponds to the sequential line network with intermediate active nodes; that is, agents are placed in a line and, every other agent, they connect with the predecessor agent and with the subsequent agent. In this way, cost accumulation is interrupted and benefits are maximized.
tldr: The paper extends a network-formation game model by allowing bidirectional information flow while connection costs remain asymmetric, and characterizes the resulting Nash and strict Nash equilibrium topologies.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize the earlier Larrosa and Tohm\'e (2003) framework, where information flowed only one way, to capture settings in which information circulates in both directions while costs are still borne solely by the initiating agent.
method: They modify the payoff function of a strategic network-formation model to include bidirectional communication, then analyze the set of Nash networks and identify which topologies satisfy the stricter strict-Nash condition.
result: Several optimal topologies remain Nash networks, but the unique strict Nash network is the sequential line network with intermediate active nodes, where every other agent connects to both its predecessor and successor, halting cost accumulation while maximizing benefits.
conclusion: Bidirectional information flow combined with asymmetric cost-bearing reshapes equilibrium network topology, favoring a sparse alternating-connection line structure as the stable configuration.

title: Strategic Information Transmission Over Gossip Networks
authors: Emirhan Tekez, Melih Bastopcu, Sinan Gezici
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a fully connected gossip network of [MATH] nodes that track a binary continuous-time Markov source through a strategic sender transmitting updates under a communication budget at a rate that depends on the source state. The receivers exchange packets through gossip and decide whether to follow the sender. We model this interaction as a Stackelberg game and analyze it through a stochastic hybrid systems (SHS) framework. We prove that the sender's budget constraint binds at every interior optimum, reducing its problem to a one-dimensional search on the budget line. When the sender pushes its preferred state at the higher rate, the receivers gossip at the highest available rate. Gossip has no direction of its own and works against the asymmetry in the sender's policy rather than reinforcing it. We prove that an optimistic Stackelberg equilibrium exists, and that it is unique and explicitly characterized whenever a policy on the strategic half of that line is feasible at the gossip cap. Monte Carlo simulations agree with the analytical recursion.
tldr: This paper studies strategic information transmission in a fully connected gossip network where nodes track a binary Markov source through a sender constrained by a state-dependent communication budget.
motivation: The work is motivated by understanding how strategic senders and gossiping receivers interact when information updates are costly and receivers can exchange information among themselves.
method: The authors model the interaction as a Stackelberg game and analyze it using a stochastic hybrid systems (SHS) framework, proving properties of the sender's budget constraint and characterizing equilibria.
result: They show that the sender's budget constraint binds at every interior optimum, reducing its problem to a one-dimensional search, and that gossip works against the sender's policy asymmetry rather than reinforcing it; an optimistic Stackelberg equilibrium is proved to exist and be unique under a feasibility condition.
conclusion: The analysis provides a game-theoretic characterization of strategic communication over gossip networks, with Monte Carlo simulations matching the analytical recursion, but it does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Empirical Evaluation Of Membership Inference Attacks On Nlp Text Classifiers: A Baseline Study On Sst-2
authors: Muhammad Abusaqer William Novak (minot State University)
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) try to determine whether a specific record was used to train a model, a privacy risk that matters in natural language processing (NLP), where training data can contain sensitive user text. This paper presents a controlled benchmark of membership inference vulnerability for text classification on the GLUE SST-2 sentiment dataset. A TF-IDF + Logistic Regression pipeline and a fine-tuned DistilBERT classifier are compared under a loss-threshold MIA, with utility measured by development accuracy and macro F1. DistilBERT reached 0.9466 accuracy and 0.9460 macro F1 against 0.8756 and 0.8727 for Logistic Regression, yet both models leaked membership signal (Attack AUC 0.5615 and 0.5800, respectively). Two mitigations were tested. Stronger regularization reduced leakage for Logistic Regression at a visible utility cost, whereas fine-tuning DistilBERT for 2 epochs instead of 3 reduced leakage with negligible accuracy loss. Lightweight training adjustments can improve the privacy-utility trade-off without complex defenses.
tldr: A benchmark study measuring membership inference attack vulnerability of TF-IDF+Logistic Regression and fine-tuned DistilBERT text classifiers on SST-2, showing both leak membership signal and that simple training adjustments can improve the privacy-utility trade-off.
motivation: Training data in NLP often contains sensitive user text, and membership inference attacks pose a privacy risk; the authors aim to establish a controlled baseline for quantifying this leakage in standard text classification models.
method: The authors compare a TF-IDF + Logistic Regression pipeline against a fine-tuned DistilBERT classifier on the GLUE SST-2 dataset, evaluating a loss-threshold MIA alongside utility metrics (development accuracy, macro F1), and test two mitigations: stronger regularization and fewer fine-tuning epochs.
result: DistilBERT achieved 0.9466 accuracy / 0.9460 macro F1 versus 0.8756 / 0.8727 for Logistic Regression, yet both leaked membership signal with attack AUCs of 0.5615 and 0.5800 respectively; stronger regularization reduced leakage for Logistic Regression at visible utility cost, while 2-epoch DistilBERT fine-tuning reduced leakage with negligible accuracy loss.
conclusion: Lightweight training adjustments can improve the privacy-utility trade-off for NLP text classifiers without resorting to complex defenses, providing a practical baseline for MIA evaluation.

title: A Four-Valued Graph Model For Conflict Resolution: Core Framework And A Machine-Checked Formalization In Lean 4
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note consolidates the core of the Quasi-Closed World Graph Model for Conflict Resolution (QCW-GMCR), which extends the standard Graph Model for Conflict Resolution with Belnap's four-valued logic to represent option-level epistemic ambiguity, and pairs the framework with a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization. QCW-GMCR combines: (1) FOUR-valued option assignments with compositional propagation to state-level feasibility; (2) graded reachability (definite, credible, possible) based on an FDE-inspired transition-warrant semantics, with definite reachability related to FDE consequence in the Boolean fragment; (3) axiomatized deterministic reductions from four-valued assessments to binary decisions, including four canonical operators reflecting distinct risk attitudes; and (4) catastrophe-avoiding equilibrium concepts with a quasi-closed-world safety invariant. A four-valued hypergame extension captures heterogeneous subjective assessments across decision makers. We state the core definitions and results and report the parts verified in Lean 4 with mathlib, including the classical GMCR stability hierarchy, algebraic and compositional properties of FOUR-valued conjunction, properties of the canonical reductions, and the graded reachability hierarchy. The formalization also helped identify and correct earlier claims, including a knowledge-monotonicity axiom replaced by truth monotonicity. This preprint provides a stable, citable record of the framework and its current formal verification status.
tldr: This paper presents a four-valued graph model for conflict resolution using Belnap logic and a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization.
motivation: The work aims to extend the standard Graph Model for Conflict Resolution to handle epistemic ambiguity at the option level, providing a formalized framework for strategic conflicts.
method: It introduces quasi-closed world four-valued option assignments, graded reachability, axiomatized reductions to binary decisions, and catastrophe-avoiding equilibria, with parts verified in Lean 4 and mathlib.
result: The framework includes a four-valued hypergame extension, verified properties of conjunction and reachability, and corrected earlier claims such as replacing a knowledge-monotonicity axiom with truth monotonicity.
conclusion: The preprint consolidates the QCW-GMCR framework and its formal verification status, offering a stable citable record for conflict resolution modeling.

title: Geometric Analysis Of Doppler-Based Navigation With Low Earth Orbit Satellites
authors: Carlos Caravaca Gallego, Pini Gurfil, Hector Rotstein
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing vulnerability of Global Navigation Satellite Systems has motivated renewed interest in Doppler-based navigation using low Earth orbit satellites, which can determine position, velocity, clock bias, and clock drift from carrier Doppler measurements. However, the geometric dilution of precision (GDOP) in this eight-state problem behaves fundamentally differently from the GDOP in pseudorange-based navigation. In particular, volume-based satellite selection, effective for pseudorange-based GDOP minimization, has been empirically found to perform poorly for Doppler GDOP. This paper establishes a geometric foundation for Doppler GDOP characterization. A closed-form geometric parameterization of the Doppler measurement Jacobian in terms of elevation, azimuth, inclination, and altitude ratio is derived. It is shown that the clock bias sensitivity depends on elevation, altitude, and the angle between the satellite velocity vector and the line of sight. This sensitivity produces a correlation with the clock drift that no geometric arrangement can remove. A Schur complement decomposition of the eight-state information matrix is performed, yielding an exact GDOP inflation formula, governed by a collinearity coefficient that measures the alignment between the clock bias column and a seven-state subspace. It is proven that the geometric coupling that renders clock bias observable is the same coupling that inflates estimation covariance, and that satellite altitude diversity reduces the collinearity by separating satellites at equal elevation onto distinct sensitivity bands. An example employing a two-shell satellite configuration illustrates the analysis.
tldr: The paper develops a geometric characterization of Doppler-based navigation using low Earth orbit satellites, showing that Doppler GDOP behaves differently from pseudorange GDOP and deriving exact inflation formulas via a Schur complement decomposition.
motivation: The vulnerability of Global Navigation Satellite Systems has renewed interest in Doppler-based navigation with LEO satellites, but geometric dilution of precision in the eight-state Doppler problem is poorly understood and conventional satellite selection methods perform badly.
method: The authors derive a closed-form geometric parameterization of the Doppler measurement Jacobian in terms of elevation, azimuth, inclination, and altitude ratio, then perform a Schur complement decomposition of the eight-state information matrix to obtain an exact GDOP inflation formula governed by a collinearity coefficient.
result: They prove that clock bias sensitivity depends on elevation, altitude, and the satellite-velocity-to-line-of-sight angle, producing an irreducible correlation with clock drift; altitude diversity reduces collinearity, as illustrated by a two-shell satellite configuration.
conclusion: Doppler-based navigation geometry fundamentally differs from pseudorange-based geometry, and volume-based satellite selection is ineffective; geometric coupling both enables clock bias observability and inflates estimation covariance.

title: The Semantic Elevation Operator And The Closure Of The Undecidable Class Under Preservation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The undecidability of a program's static semantic properties is governed by Rice's theorem. Self-modifying systems, however, require analysing not whether a property holds now, but whether it is preserved when the system rewrites itself. We formalise this transition through a semantic elevation operator {\Lambda}{\Phi}, which turns the static question "does x satisfy P?" into the dynamic question "is P preserved after x is transformed by {\Phi}?". We prove that when {\Phi} is intensional (depending on the source code, not only on the computed function), the elevated property remains undecidable even though it breaks the extensionality that Rice's theorem requires; the proof rests on Kleene's recursion theorem, not on Rice. Consequently the class U of non-verifiable properties is closed under the elevation operator. Unbounded iteration of the operator climbs the arithmetical hierarchy -to {\Pi}02-completeness- consolidating non-verifiability as a structural fact. We further show that the supervisory regress does not terminate: no fnite tower of increasingly capable verifiers yields an unconditional certificate. A categorical reading of these results in the efective topos, in which elevation appears as an instance of Lawvere's fxed-point theorem, is left as a direction for future work.
tldr: The paper introduces a semantic elevation operator that transforms static undecidable properties into dynamic preservation properties, proving closure of the undecidable class under intensional self-modification.
motivation: Self-modifying systems require analyzing whether semantic properties are preserved under rewrites, a question not covered by Rice's theorem for static properties.
method: The authors formalize the semantic elevation operator ΛΦ, prove undecidability for intensional Φ using Kleene's recursion theorem, and extend results to the arithmetical hierarchy and a categorical interpretation.
result: The elevated property remains undecidable despite breaking extensionality, the class U of non-verifiable properties is closed under elevation, and unbounded iteration reaches Π⁰₂-completeness.
conclusion: Non-verifiability is a structural fact under self-modification, with no finite tower of verifiers providing an unconditional certificate; a topos-theoretic reading via Lawvere's fixed-point theorem is suggested.

title: Mln-eigs: A Multilayer Network Framework For Solving Stackelberg Escape Interdiction Games On Dynamic Transportation Networks
authors: Sukanya Samanta, Kei Kimura, Makoto Yokoo, Palash Dey
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interdicting an escaping criminal with limited police resources on large-scale transportation networks is a challenging problem due to the dynamic nature of both attacker movement and defender deployment. This paper proposes , a multilayer network-based framework for solving dynamic escape interdiction problems formulated as a Stackelberg security game. A time-expanded multilayer network is constructed to explicitly model the temporal evolution of the transportation network and the feasible movements of both the attacker and the defenders. The attacker seeks to maximize the probability of successful escape, while the defenders aim to maximize the probability of interdiction. To efficiently compute the attacker's best response, the probabilistic escape formulation is transformed into an equivalent shortest-path problem through a logarithmic transformation, enabling the use of Dijkstra's algorithm. Since the defender best-response problem is computationally intractable, an approximation defender oracle is developed to generate high-quality defender strategies on the multilayer network. The proposed MLN-EIGS framework is benchmarked against an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP)-based Stackelberg formulation on a large real-world transportation network. Computational experiments demonstrate that MLN-EIGS consistently achieves defender utilities that closely match those of the exact MILP approach while substantially reducing computational time. These results demonstrate that the proposed MLN-EIGS framework provides an effective, computationally efficient, and scalable alternative to exact MILP-based Stackelberg optimization for large-scale dynamic escape interdiction problems.
tldr: The paper proposes MLN-EIGS, a multilayer network framework for solving dynamic Stackelberg escape interdiction games on large-scale transportation networks.
motivation: Interdicting an escaping criminal with limited police resources is challenging due to dynamic attacker movement and defender deployment on large networks.
method: It constructs a time-expanded multilayer network, transforms the attacker's probabilistic escape problem into a shortest-path problem via logarithmic transformation, and develops an approximate defender oracle for the intractable defender best-response problem.
result: MLN-EIGS achieves defender utilities close to an exact MILP-based Stackelberg formulation while substantially reducing computational time on a large real-world transportation network.
conclusion: The framework provides an effective, computationally efficient, and scalable alternative to exact MILP-based Stackelberg optimization for dynamic escape interdiction.

title: No-Box Vulnerability Analysis: Description-only Detection Of Indirect Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities In Mcp Servers
authors: Zehua Zhang, Jie Hu, Pratham Hegde, Aditya Maheshbhai Gabani, Souradip Nath, Yibo Liu, Siyu Liu, Hongkai Chen, Hulin Wang, Zhuoer Lyu, Chang Zhu, Divij Handa, Yan Shoshitaishvili, Tiffany Bao, Ruoyu Wang, Adam Doupe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional vulnerability analysis relies on either system access or dynamic interaction, all of which may be unavailable to third-party analysts auditing closed-source, remotely hosted, critical in situ systems, or commercially gated software. Therefore, we propose a new paradigm of no-box vulnerability analysis in which neither access nor runtime interaction is available, and only functionality metadata is available. Such metadata defines the intended behavior of the system, including its inputs, outputs, and side effects, while constraining the space of implementations consistent with that behavior. We propose hypothesizing about vulnerabilities that exist across all possible implementations of a given system metadata, without observing or interacting with the target system. An analyst can later validate these hypotheses when additional access is available. We showcase the feasibility of no-box vulnerability analysis through implementing a prototype called MCPSEC, which audits Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities using only the tool metadata exposed at server registration time. We evaluate MCPSEC on 20 widely deployed MCP servers comprising 177 tools, among which human evaluators confirm 95 vulnerable tools. MCPSEC identified 143 tools as vulnerable, and for each vulnerable tool, it produced a hypothesized vulnerability along with exploitation technique. Using metadata alone, MCPSEC predicted 94 (98.9% recall) real verified vulnerabilities, compared against an LLM baseline with 80 (84.2% recall). Overall, our results introduce no-box vulnerability analysis as a new analysis paradigm and demonstrate its practical feasibility in realistic systems.
tldr: The paper introduces 'no-box vulnerability analysis' and demonstrates it via MCPSEC, a tool that detects indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities in MCP servers using only registration-time metadata.
motivation: Third-party analysts often cannot access or interact with closed-source, remotely hosted, or commercially gated systems, creating a need for vulnerability detection without system access or runtime interaction.
method: The authors formalize a no-box paradigm where only functionality metadata is available, then implement MCPSEC to audit MCP server tool metadata and hypothesize vulnerabilities that hold across all implementations consistent with that metadata.
result: Evaluated on 20 widely deployed MCP servers with 177 tools, MCPSEC identified 143 vulnerable tools, predicting 94 of 95 human-verified vulnerabilities (98.9% recall), outperforming an LLM baseline with 84.2% recall.
conclusion: The work establishes no-box vulnerability analysis as a new paradigm and shows its practical feasibility for detecting indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities in MCP servers.

title: Occupancy-Domain Over-the-Air Computation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) aggregates distributed data through the wireless multiple-access channel, but coherent implementations require channel state information (CSI), phase alignment, and power control, whereas non-coherent energy methods remain affected by fading. Signal superposition at the receive antenna is linear but requires coherence, and energy superposition is linear only in expectation over fading. We introduce occupancy-domain computation (ODC), whose observable is neither a received amplitude nor an energy: the sum is carried by the silence of the shared resources. With exponential Bernoulli activation, the individual silence probabilities multiply, and the server recovers the sum from the idle fraction using binary activity decisions alone, so that once an activation is detected the amplitude that produced it does not enter the estimate. We characterize the maximum-likelihood estimator, optimal load, and a scale-integrated Fisher-information bound for non-adaptive operation over unknown dynamic ranges. We then introduce balanced occupancy computation (BOC), where each device forms a data-dependent quota of random burst placements. This removes the random placement-count fluctuation of Bernoulli activation; under ideal detection, the leading-order asymptotic root-mean-square error of BOC is no larger than that of Bernoulli ODC at any load and approaches [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of resource elements, as the number of devices becomes small relative to [MATH]. We further analyze unknown-scale operation, finite-frame deviations, and heterogeneous detection misses. Simulations validate the theory and compare ODC/BOC with affine non-coherent energy aggregation and REED.
tldr: The paper introduces occupancy-domain over-the-air computation (ODC/BOC), a classical wireless aggregation scheme that encodes sums in silence probabilities rather than coherent amplitudes or energies.
motivation: AirComp typically requires CSI, phase alignment, and power control for coherent superposition, while non-coherent energy methods are affected by fading and scale uncertainty.
method: The authors define occupancy-domain computation using exponential Bernoulli activation so silence probabilities multiply, derive the ML estimator, optimal load, and a Fisher-information bound, and propose balanced occupancy computation (BOC) with data-dependent burst placements to reduce fluctuation.
result: BOC removes random placement-count fluctuation of Bernoulli ODC, has leading-order asymptotic RMSE no larger than Bernoulli ODC at any load, and approaches a resource-element-dependent bound as device count becomes small relative to resources; simulations validate the theory and compare with affine non-coherent energy aggregation and REED.
conclusion: Occupancy-domain computation offers a non-coherent AirComp alternative robust to unknown dynamic ranges and fading, with BOC improving accuracy and providing theoretical benchmarks for future wireless aggregation designs.

title: A Proof Of Cairns' Conjecture About Geodesic Triangulations Of The 2-sphere
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper contains a detailed proof of a 1941 conjecture of S.S. Cairns concerning the space of geodesic triangulations of the 2-sphere. The methods are neither combinatorical nor Riemannian but belong to differential topology.
tldr: The paper provides a detailed differential-topology proof of Cairns' 1941 conjecture on the space of geodesic triangulations of the 2-sphere.
motivation: Cairns conjectured in 1941 a structural property of the space of geodesic triangulations of the 2-sphere, and a complete rigorous proof had remained outstanding.
method: The proof uses techniques from differential topology rather than combinatorial or Riemannian methods.
result: A full proof of Cairns' conjecture is established, characterizing the connectivity/structure of the space of geodesic triangulations on the 2-sphere.
conclusion: The work resolves a long-standing conjecture in geometric topology, though it lies entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: A General Approach To Enharmonicism
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a general approach to enharmonicism within syntactic music theory; that is, we formalize several abstract structures of enharmonicism without any acoustic considerations. The structures of concern to this paper are constructed from diatonics, chromatics, and enharmonics, and we seek to present a general enharmonic theory that builds upon Hook's enharmonic theory published in "Enharmonic Systems: A Theory of Key Signatures, Enharmonic Equivalence and Diatonicism" (2007). We also propose that the two criteria of reflection and maximal evenness can be used to determine whether an arbitrary enharmonic system is musically practical. Moreover, we argue that preferential treatment of the standard enharmonic system (SES) can be motivated from an abstract mathematical perspective divorced from pitch consideration and conventional acoustic constructions of SES.
tldr: The paper proposes a general syntactic theory of enharmonicism, formalizing abstract structures from diatonics, chromatics, and enharmonics without acoustic considerations.
motivation: It aims to build upon Hook's enharmonic theory and to determine whether an arbitrary enharmonic system is musically practical using the criteria of reflection and maximal evenness.
method: The author constructs abstract mathematical structures of enharmonicism and argues that preferential treatment of the standard enharmonic system can be motivated from an abstract perspective divorced from pitch and acoustics.
result: The paper presents a general enharmonic theory and proposes reflection and maximal evenness as criteria for musical practicality of enharmonic systems.
conclusion: Enharmonicism can be studied formally within syntactic music theory, and the standard enharmonic system may be justified through abstract mathematical principles rather than acoustic constructions.

title: Some Properties Of Mordukhovich Derivatives With Applications To Locally Variational Inequalities In Banach Spaces
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we will investigate the connection between Frechet derivatives and Mordukhovich derivatives of single-valued mappings in Banach spaces. We will find some properties of Mordukhovich derivatives of set-valued mappings, which will be demonstrated by the set-valued metric projection operator in finite dimensional Banach spaces. We introduce the concept of locally variational inequalities in Banach spaces, which focus on finding solutions within some specific neighborhoods rather than across the entire global domain; and we find the connection between the solutions of locally variational inequality problems and the Mordukhovich derivatives.
tldr: The paper studies properties of Mordukhovich derivatives of single-valued and set-valued mappings in Banach spaces and applies them to a newly introduced class of locally variational inequalities.
motivation: Mordukhovich derivatives generalize Fréchet derivatives to nonsmooth and set-valued settings, and the authors aim to clarify their structure and connect them to local solvability of variational inequalities.
method: Purely analytical techniques in Banach space nonsmooth analysis: comparison of Fréchet and Mordukhovich derivatives, derivation of structural properties, illustration via the set-valued metric projection operator in finite dimensions, and formulation of locally variational inequalities.
result: Several properties of Mordukhovich derivatives of set-valued mappings are established, and a link is derived between solutions of locally variational inequality problems and Mordukhovich derivatives.
conclusion: The work extends nonsmooth variational analysis in Banach spaces with a local variational inequality framework, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quadrature By Matched Asymptotic Expansion (qbmax): Accelerating Evaluation Of Layer Potentials With Boundary Layers
authors: Chaoqi Lin, Xiaoyu Wei, Andreas Kl\"ockner
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating layer potentials with rapidly decaying kernels becomes computationally challenging in the presence of boundary layers, as occurs for Helmholtz layer potentials with large imaginary wavenumbers. We introduce Quadrature by Matched Asymptotic Expansion (QBMAX), a high-order method that extends the Quadrature by Expansion (QBX) framework by incorporating the kernel's asymptotic decay behavior directly into the Taylor expansion of the potential. Numerical results in both 2D and 3D show improvements of up to four digits over QBX for the tested large-parameter cases, while the methods can perform similarly for smaller parameters or more strongly curved geometries. A symbolic weighted operation-count model indicates comparable costs for forming the two expansion kernels. The Taylor expansions have the same formal order, while QBMAX reduces the truncation-error constants in the flat-boundary model and generally exhibits less convergence degradation in the reported experiments.
tldr: QBMAX is a high-order numerical quadrature method that incorporates kernel asymptotic decay into Taylor expansions to accelerate evaluation of layer potentials in boundary-layer regimes.
motivation: Evaluating layer potentials with rapidly decaying kernels (e.g. Helmholtz with large imaginary wavenumber) is computationally costly when boundary layers are present, motivating an improved expansion-based quadrature scheme.
method: The authors extend the Quadrature by Expansion (QBX) framework by embedding matched asymptotic decay behavior of the kernel directly into the Taylor expansion of the potential, analyzed via a symbolic weighted operation-count model.
result: Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D show up to four-digit accuracy improvements over QBX for large-parameter cases, with comparable computational costs for forming the expansion kernels and reduced truncation-error constants in flat-boundary models.
conclusion: QBMAX offers a systematic way to retain high-order accuracy in boundary-layer settings where standard QBX degrades, though benefits diminish for smaller parameters or strongly curved geometries.

title: The Elliptically Optimal Confidence Interval: A Bivariate Extension Of Wilson's Score Method
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constructing a confidence interval for the difference between two independent binomial proportions involves a nuisance direction that is not identified by the estimand. The one-sample Wilson score interval inverts a scalar score test, but has no direct bivariate analogue isolating the difference: inverting the joint normal approximation yields an elliptical region in the unit square, whereas the estimand \(p_1-p_2\) is one-dimensional. We define the Elliptically Optimal (EO) confidence interval as the range of \(p_1-p_2\) over this region and solve the resulting optimization problem in closed form, obtaining explicit bounds in six mutually exclusive and exhaustive cases. The solution admits a compact characterization: the EO interval is the score interval obtained by maximizing over the nuisance variance rather than estimating it. It is therefore the shortest interval obtained by projecting the elliptical region, and inherits its coverage guarantee. We derive the exact coverage excess, \(2[\Phi(z)-\Phi(z)]\), where \(\) is the ratio of the least-favourable to the true standard deviation. The excess vanishes on an explicit line through the parameter space, is bounded by \(\alpha\), and is invariant under proportional scaling of the sample sizes. Exact enumeration of the binomial coverage shows that the Wald interval, whose variance estimator is downward biased by a factor \(1-1/n\) under balanced allocation, falls below nominal coverage almost everywhere. The EO interval never under-covers under the normal approximation and always yields admissible, non-degenerate bounds. Its price is over-coverage when both proportions are extreme, which we quantify exactly.
tldr: The paper introduces an Elliptically Optimal confidence interval for the difference between two independent binomial proportions, derived by projecting an elliptical confidence region for the joint proportions onto the difference.
motivation: Standard one-sample Wilson score intervals do not have a direct bivariate analogue for the difference of two proportions, and the Wald interval often under-covers in this setting.
method: The authors define the Elliptically Optimal interval as the range of the difference over the elliptical region obtained by inverting the joint normal approximation, solve it in closed form across six cases, and compare coverage to Wald and score intervals.
result: The EO interval is the shortest projection of the elliptical region, inherits its coverage guarantee, never under-covers under the normal approximation, and has an exact over-coverage excess that vanishes on an explicit line and is bounded by alpha.
conclusion: The EO interval provides a principled, admissible, non-degenerate alternative for the difference of binomial proportions, at the cost of over-coverage when both proportions are extreme.

title: The Privacy Subsidy In Market Microstructure
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy-preserving exchange designs price on a coarsened view of order flow. We show that a market maker committed to informationally efficient (posterior-mean) pricing on a signal strictly coarser than the flow it settles necessarily cedes a closed-form welfare transfer to traders -- the privacy subsidy -- and that no rule restricted to the coarse signal is simultaneously efficient and zero-profit against the settled flow. We establish this impossibility for a general coarsening, then characterise the subsidy in closed form across three canonical microstructure models: single-period Kyle with Gaussian flow noise, Glosten-Milgrom with a binary direction channel, and continuous-time Kyle-Back with a Brownian channel. The subsidy obeys a structural correspondence with Loss-Versus-Rebalancing, both welfare rates factorising as a squared noise driver times a committed-object factor. Gross of fees the subsidy is a pure transfer recovered by a break-even fee; once levied, that fee distorts volume, and the resulting deadweight -- under an explicit allocative value of trade -- is fourth-order in the noise scale while the gross subsidy is second-order, so privacy is welfare-neutral to leading order with a strictly smaller irrecoverable loss. Endogenising the privacy level, a protocol trading a differential-privacy benefit against this deadweight chooses an interior noise scale in closed form; doing so leaves the half-revealing product of price impact and informed intensity intact while unpinning the volatility-elasticity of price impact from its textbook value of one.
tldr: The paper introduces a 'privacy subsidy' in market microstructure, showing that market makers pricing on coarsened order flow must cede a welfare transfer, with optimal privacy balancing differential-privacy benefits against deadweight loss.
motivation: Privacy-preserving exchange designs force market makers to price on coarse signals rather than full order flow, raising questions about efficiency, welfare transfers, and the cost of privacy.
method: The authors derive an impossibility result for general coarsening and characterize the subsidy in closed form across three canonical models: single-period Kyle, Glosten-Milgrom, and continuous-time Kyle-Back, including an endogenized privacy level via a differential-privacy tradeoff.
result: The subsidy corresponds structurally to Loss-Versus-Rebalancing, is second-order in noise scale, while the deadweight loss from fees is fourth-order, making privacy welfare-neutral to leading order; optimal interior noise leaves half-revealing price impact intact but unpins volatility-elasticity from one.
conclusion: Privacy in market microstructure entails a welfare transfer that can be recovered by fees, but the resulting deadweight loss is smaller by orders of magnitude, and endogenizing privacy yields a closed-form optimal noise scale with implications for price impact.

title: AspisAI: A Canonical, Machine-Interpretable Governance Framework For Automated Multi-Standard Compliance Monitoring
authors: Tsafac Nkombong Regine Cyrille, Hasan Dag, Reiner Creutzburg, Knut Haufe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organisations operating in regulated and critical-infrastructure sectors must satisfy multiple, heterogeneous cybersecurity and privacy instruments simultaneously, including but not limited to ISO/IEC~27001, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework~2.0, Cyber Essentials, and the GDPR. In practice, these obligations are managed through manual mappings, spreadsheet-based tracking, and periodic audits that are costly to maintain, inconsistent across standards, and weak in traceability. This paper presents , a bounded, standard-agnostic governance framework that translates selected requirements from several frameworks into a canonical, machine-interpretable control model, and evaluates submitted evidence against condition-based decision rules to produce explainable, traceable compliance determinations. Within a bounded scope of 26 representative requirements, the framework is evaluated in a controlled simulation against five governance-oriented criteria and, critically, against two external reference points that mitigate the circularity of single-author evaluation: its cross-standard mappings are validated against NIST's own published informative references, with 57\,\% exact agreement and divergences confined to same-family controls, and the framework is applied to real third-party evidence from the OpenSSF Scorecard, surfacing genuine governance gaps in a live open-source project. The controlled results, comprising full requirement encoding, 88.5\,\% mapping coverage, complete traceability, and correct detection of all introduced gaps, establish functional correctness, while the external validation provides evidence of applicability beyond the simulation. The contribution is therefore a demonstration that a canonical, provenance-preserving governance model can render multi-standard compliance both automatable and auditable.
tldr: AspisAI is a governance framework that encodes cybersecurity and privacy requirements (ISO/IEC 27001, NIST CSF 2.0, Cyber Essentials, GDPR) into a canonical machine-interpretable control model to automate and audit multi-standard compliance.
motivation: Organisations in regulated sectors must satisfy many heterogeneous security and privacy instruments simultaneously, yet current practice relies on manual mappings, spreadsheets, and periodic audits that are costly, inconsistent, and poorly traceable.
method: The authors define a bounded, standard-agnostic control model translating 26 representative requirements into condition-based decision rules, then evaluate it in a controlled simulation against five governance criteria plus external validation against NIST's published informative references and OpenSSF Scorecard evidence from a live open-source project.
result: The framework achieves full requirement encoding, 88.5% mapping coverage, complete traceability, correct detection of all introduced gaps, and 57% exact agreement with NIST informative references, with divergences limited to same-family controls.
conclusion: A canonical, provenance-preserving governance model can make multi-standard compliance both automatable and auditable, offering a generic and explainable alternative to manual compliance tracking.

title: Stv Audit Graphs: A Visual Tool To Measure Election Stability
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Single Transferable Vote (STV) is an algorithmic election rule. Round by round, a profile of ranked-choice ballots is reinterpreted to determine which decision to make next, and candidates are seated or eliminated until a full winner set emerges. This algorithmic nature makes STV theoretically more brittle than other election rules: uncertainty about an early round of the election might percolate irreversibly into the rest. For this reason, a generalized non-trivial Risk-Limiting Audit (RLA) framework has remained elusive for STV. Such a framework must concoct a set of null hypotheses, or assertions, whose rejection would bound the probability that the outcome of the election was incorrectly reported. We present audit graphs as a solution to design the assertions needed for RLAs of arbitrary STV elections, as well as quantitatively describe the uncertainty (or lack thereof) of their outcomes. These audit graphs explore election paths that are ``close'' to the recorded one by considering the alternative decisions the STV algorithm might have made if a small number of ballots were perturbed.
tldr: The paper introduces 'audit graphs' as a visual and quantitative tool for designing risk-limiting audits of Single Transferable Vote (STV) elections by exploring perturbed election paths.
motivation: STV's round-by-round algorithmic nature makes it brittle: early-round uncertainty can irreversibly propagate to the final winner set, which has made a general Risk-Limiting Audit (RLA) framework for STV elusive.
method: The author constructs audit graphs that enumerate election paths 'close' to the recorded outcome by considering alternative STV decisions under small perturbations of ballots, yielding assertions whose rejection bounds the probability of an incorrectly reported outcome.
result: Audit graphs provide a systematic way to design the null hypotheses/assertions needed for RLAs of arbitrary STV elections and to quantitatively characterize the uncertainty of their outcomes.
conclusion: The framework generalizes RLA design to STV elections, offering a practical visual and quantitative tool for election stability analysis.

title: You've Got A Bud In Me: Authenticated Reads From Per-Block Write Logs
authors: Alejandro Ranchal-Pedrosa, Cody Littley, Ben Marsh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchains usually pay for authenticated reads by maintaining a structure that spans the entire state. We show how validators can support historical membership and exclusion proofs by authenticating each block's writes instead. A Block Update Digest (BUD) commits a write log whose predecessor pointers link successive modifications of each key. A SuperBUD summarizes last writes over a window; an exponential hierarchy turns long unchanged intervals into short proofs. The digest count is logarithmic in the gap within the hierarchy's range, with one additional digest per top-level window beyond it. We prove soundness against adversarial provers and up to f Byzantine validators, and completeness for queries anchored by a post-deployment modification, assuming archive, attestation, and committee evidence is available. Across a 50x increase in state size, the measured base-BUD path rises by 1.24x, compared with 3.1x and 69.5x for in-memory and cache-bounded disk-backed Merkle Patricia tries. On the synthetic trace, two-digest read-layer payloads stay below 800 bytes, and warm hash-path verification takes at most 146 microseconds at p99.
tldr: The paper proposes authenticating per-block write logs (Block Update Digests and a SuperBUD hierarchy) to provide cheap historical membership and exclusion proofs in blockchain state, instead of spanning the entire state with a Merkle Patricia trie.
motivation: Blockchains normally maintain a global authenticated data structure spanning all state, which makes historical membership and exclusion proofs expensive as state grows.
method: Each block's writes are committed in a Block Update Digest whose predecessor pointers chain successive modifications of each key; a SuperBUD summarizes last writes over a window, and an exponential hierarchy compresses long unchanged intervals into short proofs with logarithmic digest counts.
result: Soundness is proven against adversarial provers and up to f Byzantine validators, with measured base-BUD path growth of only 1.24x across a 50x state-size increase, versus 3.1x and 69.5x for in-memory and cache-bounded disk-backed Merkle Patricia tries; read payloads stay under 800 bytes and hash-path verification is at most 146 microseconds at p99.
conclusion: Per-block write-log authentication offers a scalable alternative to global state-wide authenticated structures for historical read proofs in blockchains, though it relies on archive, attestation, and committee evidence.

title: Two-step High-accuracy Microwave Frequency Measurement And Time-frequency Analysis Based On Optical Frequency Combs
authors: Wentao Ma, Taixia Shi, Chi Jiang, Yang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband microwave frequency measurement and time-frequency analysis are crucial for applications such as electronic warfare. However, when it comes to ultra wideband signal analysis, traditional electronic methods have high analysis accuracy, but intrinsic electronic bottlenecks limit their real-time analysis. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a two-step microwave frequency measurement and time-frequency analysis method based on optical frequency combs. The system first performs coarse frequency localization over the 0-40 GHz range using stimulated-Brillouin-scattering-assisted frequency-to-time mapping (FTTM) and dual-comb channelized reception. The dual-comb is then reapplied for downconverting the signal under test, followed by digital signal processing to achieve high-accuracy unambiguous frequency extraction. Experimental results show that the system achieves mean single-tone frequency measurement errors of less than 10 kHz over 0-40 GHz. We further experimentally measure multi-tone, linearly frequency-modulated, and V-shaped frequency-modulated signals, demonstrating the proposed method's capability for analyzing complex signals.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a two-step optical-frequency-comb-based method for broadband microwave frequency measurement and time-frequency analysis, achieving sub-10 kHz single-tone frequency errors over 0–40 GHz.
motivation: Ultra-wideband microwave signal analysis is important for applications such as electronic warfare, but traditional electronic methods are limited in real-time analysis due to intrinsic electronic bottlenecks.
method: The system first performs coarse frequency localization over 0–40 GHz using stimulated-Brillouin-scattering-assisted frequency-to-time mapping and dual-comb channelized reception, then uses the dual-comb for downconversion followed by digital signal processing for high-accuracy unambiguous frequency extraction.
result: Experimental results show mean single-tone frequency measurement errors of less than 10 kHz over 0–40 GHz, and the method successfully measures multi-tone, linearly frequency-modulated, and V-shaped frequency-modulated signals.
conclusion: The proposed two-step approach enables high-accuracy broadband microwave frequency measurement and complex signal analysis using optical frequency combs, offering a potential alternative to electronic methods for real-time ultra-wideband signal processing.

title: A Geometrically Parameterized Quasi-Stationary 3d Model For High-Frequency Induction Tube Welding
authors: Dmitry Ivanov, John Inge Asperheim, Bj{\o}rnar Grande, Prerana Das
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A three-dimensional multiphysics finite element framework for the simulation of high-frequency induction welding of tubes is presented. The model couples a time-harmonic magnetic scalar potential formulation with a stabilized quasi-stationary advection-diffusion heat transport equation, enabling accurate prediction of electromagnetic and thermal fields under industrial operating conditions. The framework incorporates parameterized geometry generation and semi-automated, physics-tailored mesh construction and is implemented using the open-source tools GetDP and Gmsh. Validation against measurements from a commercial induction welding line for AISI 304 stainless steel tubes demonstrates good agreement with operating data. The validated model is subsequently applied to investigate the influence of impeder material by comparing a conventional FeNiZnV ferrite with the soft magnetic composite Ferrotron 559H for the induction welding of AISI 304 stainless steel tubes.
tldr: The paper presents a three-dimensional multiphysics finite-element framework for simulating high-frequency induction tube welding, coupling time-harmonic electromagnetic fields with a stabilized quasi-stationary heat transport equation.
motivation: Industrial induction welding of tubes requires accurate prediction of electromagnetic and thermal fields to optimize process parameters and impeder material selection.
method: A geometrically parameterized 3D model couples a time-harmonic magnetic scalar potential formulation with an advection-diffusion heat equation, implemented in open-source GetDP and Gmsh with physics-tailored meshing.
result: The model is validated against measurements from a commercial induction welding line for AISI 304 stainless steel, showing good agreement, and is used to compare FeNiZnV ferrite with Ferrotron 559H impeders.
conclusion: The framework provides a validated computational tool for induction tube welding, but it is a classical engineering/manufacturing application with no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, or quantum platforms.

title: A Two-Mirror Faceted Projection System For Euv Lithography
authors: Vasiliy A. Es'kin, Egor V. Ivanov, Olga V. Martynova
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an all-reflective two-mirror projection system for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography operating at exposure wavelengths of [MATH]~nm (Mo/Si) and [MATH]~nm (Ru/Be), delivering a fourfold ([MATH]) demagnification of the periodic mask pattern at a numerical aperture approaching unity ([MATH]). In contrast to conventional EUV projection objectives that incorporate 6--10 aspheric mirrors with an overall optical throughput of less than [MATH], the proposed design redirects each accepted discrete spatial diffraction order scattered by the mask onto the wafer via a dedicated pair of planar mirror facets. The number of reflections is strictly fixed at two for all accepted orders, retaining [MATH]--[MATH] of the power leaving the mask in each accepted order. We derive a spatial geometry providing rigorous optical path length equalization across all diffraction orders, thereby removing order-dependent propagation phase shifts. Individually optimized 30-bilayer Bragg multilayer coatings are designed for each facet using the transfer matrix method combined with global evolutionary optimization algorithms. The architecture is generalized to a three-dimensional vector formulation with a two-dimensionally periodic mask. Utilizing inverse lithography technology, Fourier parameterization, and a differentiable electromagnetic modal waveguide solver, we solve the synthesis problem for binary absorber masks (La absorber on a Ru/Be/Sr multilayer mirror). We demonstrate simulated aerial images of sub-10-nm features on the wafer (isolated peaks with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of approximately [MATH]~nm and line pairs with a critical dimension of [MATH]~nm) and find that the two peaks remain resolved for the tested wafer defocus values from [MATH] to [MATH]~nm along the [MATH]-axis.
tldr: The paper proposes an all-reflective two-mirror faceted projection system for EUV lithography that achieves fourfold demagnification and near-unity numerical aperture with only two reflections.
motivation: Conventional EUV projection objectives use 6–10 aspheric mirrors and suffer from low optical throughput, motivating a simpler high-efficiency design.
method: The authors design a two-mirror faceted projection system with planar mirror facets, optimized 30-bilayer Bragg multilayer coatings via transfer matrix and evolutionary algorithms, and a 3D vector formulation combined with inverse lithography and a differentiable electromagnetic modal waveguide solver.
result: Simulated aerial images show sub-10-nm features, including isolated peaks with FWHM around a few nanometers and line pairs with critical dimensions below 10 nm, remaining resolved over tested wafer defocus values.
conclusion: The architecture may enable high-NA EUV lithography with fewer reflections and improved power throughput, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Disturbance Rejection For Classes Of Nonlinear Systems
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of non-adaptive global robust disturbance rejection for two distinct classes of nonlinear systems. The first class, denoted by C1, consists of nonlinear systems in strict-feedback form, with linear and Hurwitz zero-dynamics (whose states are unavailable for feedback), and enhanced - within this work - by forcing, unmatched, additive disturbances. Nonlinear tools are herein employed to demonstrate that the proposed control architecture - based on the high-gain paradigm - achieves closed-loop input-to-state stability with respect to the forcing disturbances, along with global asymptotic convergence towards an attractor which can be rendered as small as desired. Then, owing to the established input-to-state stability property, a uniformly bounded control action is additionally embedded within the control architecture. The additional unit, designed following the sliding-mode paradigm, is aimed at improving the disturbance rejection task, by potentially lowering the required high-gain control expenditure. The second class of systems, denoted by C2, is constituted by minimum-phase, uncertain, nonlinear systems with relative degree greater than one, featuring possibly unbounded, with possibly unbounded derivatives, output-dependent nonlinearities, with matched additive forcing disturbances. To solve the problem of output-feedback, non-adaptive, global robust disturbance rejection for systems within C2, first, an open-loop observer is employed in lieu of a classic dynamic extension adopted in earlier works, as the latter is no longer implementable due to the presence of unknown forcing disturbances. Subsequently, the results derived for C1 are then adapted to C2, to yield an output-feedback dynamic controller providing closed-loop global uniform boundedness, along with asymptotic regulation towards an attractor which can be rendered as small as desired.
tldr: The paper develops high-gain and sliding-mode control architectures for non-adaptive global robust disturbance rejection in two classes of nonlinear systems (strict-feedback with Hurwitz zero-dynamics, and minimum-phase uncertain systems with relative degree greater than one).
motivation: Robust disturbance rejection is a classical problem in nonlinear control, motivating architectures that achieve input-to-state stability and arbitrarily small attractors without requiring adaptation or full state feedback.
method: High-gain observer/controller design combined with an extra sliding-mode unit and an open-loop observer (instead of a classic dynamic extension) to handle unmatched and matched additive disturbances in output-feedback settings.
result: Closed-loop input-to-state stability and global uniform boundedness are proven, with asymptotic convergence to an attractor that can be rendered arbitrarily small while keeping the control action uniformly bounded.
conclusion: The proposed architectures extend disturbance rejection to broader nonlinear system classes, improving performance while potentially reducing high-gain control expenditure.

title: Constructing Pareto Sets Using Noether's Second Theorem
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an analytical approach to constructing the Pareto set in multiobjective variational control problems, based on Noether's second theorem. A fundamental connection is established between the gauge symmetries of the dynamical system describing the plant and the structure of the Pareto set. It is shown that the Pareto front can be interpreted as a conservation law arising from the invariance of the system and the quality criteria with respect to a symmetry group. A gauge regularization concept is proposed, which allows eliminating variables that do not affect the criteria without changing the Pareto set, thereby reducing the dimension of the solution space. Numerical examples are provided for the linear-quadratic regulator with two conflicting criteria and for the standard ZDT1 test problem.
tldr: The paper uses Noether's second theorem to analytically construct Pareto sets in multiobjective variational control problems.
motivation: Pareto front construction in multiobjective optimal control is typically challenging, and the authors seek an analytical symmetry-based method.
method: They connect gauge symmetries of the dynamical system to the Pareto set structure using Noether's second theorem, and propose gauge regularization to eliminate irrelevant variables.
result: The Pareto front is interpreted as a conservation law from invariance under a symmetry group, with numerical examples for a linear-quadratic regulator and the ZDT1 test problem.
conclusion: The approach provides a symmetry-based analytical framework for Pareto set construction and dimension reduction, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Vectorial Lattice Boltzmann Solver For Compressible Inviscid Flows With Generic Equation Of State
authors: I. V. Karlin S. A. Hosseini
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a vectorial lattice Boltzmann model with a space-time adaptive relaxation coefficient, combined with adaptive time-stepping for compressible Euler dynamics with generic equation of state. The model, due to special form of the relaxation coefficient devised here is shown to converge to the Euler limit with second-order accuracy in the absence of shocks under acoustic scaling. The solver is robust and able to properly capture compressible gas dynamics for both ideal and non-ideal equations of state, including the Bethe--Zel'dovich--Thompson regime. This is verified and demonstrated through a variety of configurations of increasing complexity.
tldr: A vectorial lattice Boltzmann solver with adaptive relaxation and time-stepping is developed for compressible inviscid flows with generic equations of state.
motivation: The paper aims to extend lattice Boltzmann methods to compressible Euler dynamics with non-ideal equations of state, including the Bethe-Zel'dovich-Thompson regime.
method: A space-time adaptive relaxation coefficient is combined with adaptive time-stepping within a vectorial lattice Boltzmann model to converge to the Euler limit with second-order accuracy under acoustic scaling.
result: The solver robustly captures compressible gas dynamics for ideal and non-ideal equations of state, verified across configurations of increasing complexity.
conclusion: The proposed lattice Boltzmann solver provides an accurate and robust numerical tool for compressible inviscid flows with generic equations of state.

title: Generalized Tri-circular Projections On Some Vector-valued Spaces Of Analytic Functions
authors: Hemant Kumar, Himanshu Kumar, Abdullah Bin Abu Baker
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we characterize generalized tri-circular projections on the following three vector-valued spaces of analytic functions on the open unit disk [MATH]: the Hardy space [MATH] for a complex separable Hilbert space [MATH] and [MATH]; the space [MATH] of [MATH]-valued bounded analytic functions for a Banach space [MATH] with trivial multiplier algebra; and the little Bloch spaces [MATH] and [MATH], for [MATH] smooth, strictly convex, and reflexive.
tldr: The paper characterizes generalized tri-circular projections on vector-valued spaces of analytic functions, including Hardy spaces, spaces of bounded analytic functions, and little Bloch spaces.
motivation: The study of projections on spaces of analytic functions is a classical problem in operator theory and functional analysis, and its generalization to vector-valued settings is of interest in that mathematical community.
method: The authors use functional-analytic and operator-theoretic techniques to characterize generalized tri-circular projections on Hardy spaces, Banach-valued bounded analytic function spaces with trivial multiplier algebra, and little Bloch spaces.
result: Generalized tri-circular projections are fully characterized on these three classes of vector-valued analytic function spaces under the stated assumptions on the underlying Hilbert/Banach spaces.
conclusion: The results extend classical projection theory to vector-valued analytic function spaces, contributing to pure operator theory on function spaces.

title: Antitonicity Property Of The Moore-Penrose Inverse For Selfadjoint Operators
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we study the antitonicity property of the Moore-Penrose inverse in the class of selfadjoint operators, with respect to the L\"owner order. For this purpose, we employ different positive decompositions that selfadjoint operators admit. In addition, we relate a weak version of the antitonicity property with Thompson components.
tldr: The paper studies the antitonicity property of the Moore-Penrose inverse within the class of selfadjoint operators under the Löwner order, using positive decompositions and relating a weak form of the property to Thompson components.
motivation: Antitonicity of generalized inverses is a classical question in operator theory and matrix analysis, and understanding it for selfadjoint operators under the Löwner order refines the ordering theory of positive operators.
method: The authors employ various positive decompositions that selfadjoint operators admit, and connect a weak version of the antitonicity property with Thompson components.
result: Conditions under which the Moore-Penrose inverse reverses the Löwner order for selfadjoint operators are characterized, with Thompson components providing an alternative formulation of a weak antitonicity.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of monotonicity/antitonicity of generalized inverses in operator algebra, but remains a purely mathematical operator-theoretic contribution without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Perspectives On The Unit Distance Problem
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a survey on an old open problem in combinatorics called the unit distance problem, and the field of mathematics around it, called incidence geometry. What do we know about the problem? Why is it difficult? How does it connect with other parts of math?
tldr: A survey of the unit distance problem in combinatorics and the surrounding field of incidence geometry, covering known results, difficulties, and connections to other mathematics.
motivation: The unit distance problem is a longstanding open problem in combinatorial geometry, and the author aims to explain its current state and why it resists resolution.
method: Survey/expository presentation, synthesizing known bounds, techniques from incidence geometry, and connections to other branches of mathematics.
result: A consolidated overview of what is known about the unit distance problem, its obstacles, and its relationships to adjacent areas of mathematics.
conclusion: The survey provides a conceptual map for researchers interested in combinatorial geometry, but offers no results relating to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Compact Counterexample To Su\'arez's Berezin Approximation Question
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the unweighted Bergman space and write [MATH] for the map induced by the [MATH]th higher-order Berezin transform. Su\'arez asked in 2005 whether [MATH] converges to [MATH] in operator norm for every [MATH] in the full Bergman Toeplitz algebra. We answer this question negatively in a strong form: there is a compact operator [MATH] such that \[ \sup_{m\geq 0}\|Q_m(S)\|=\infty. \] In particular, along a strictly increasing sequence [MATH] one has \[ \|Q_{m_n}(S)-S\|\longrightarrow\infty. \] The obstruction is a moving matrix edge. The proof uses a moving family of rank-one test operators, each supported in the [MATH]th matrix column. Near the corresponding edge, these test operators are sent to weighted Hankel matrices, and the limiting coefficients form an explicit Pascal kernel. We prove a standalone Pascal--Hankel theorem showing that the associated weighted Hankel transformation fails to map [MATH] boundedly into trace class. Finite-section convergence, trace duality, and the Uniform Boundedness Principle then transfer this instability to the exact Bergman maps.
tldr: The paper constructs a compact operator in the Bergman Toeplitz algebra for which the higher-order Berezin transforms do not converge in operator norm, answering Suárez's 2005 question negatively.
motivation: Suárez asked whether higher-order Berezin transforms converge in operator norm for every element of the full Bergman Toeplitz algebra, and this paper resolves that question in the negative.
method: The authors use a moving family of rank-one test operators supported in matrix columns, reduce the obstruction to a weighted Hankel transformation, prove a standalone Pascal–Hankel theorem, and then transfer the instability via finite-section convergence, trace duality, and the Uniform Boundedness Principle.
result: There exists a compact operator S such that sup_m ||Q_m(S)|| = infinity and, along a strictly increasing sequence, ||Q_{m_n}(S) - S|| diverges to infinity.
conclusion: The Berezin approximation question has a strong negative answer, with the obstruction identified as a moving matrix edge and an explicit Pascal kernel.

title: The Three-vortex System: Hopf Fibration, Symplectic Reduction, And Near-collisions
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamics of collisions and near-collisions in the system of three point vortices in the plane. The dynamics is known to be completely integrable and can be reduced to the study of Hamiltonian systems on two-dimensional symplectic leaves. This still allows for interesting behavior of the solutions, various aspects of which have been investigated in a large body of work by many authors. Our focus will be on collisions and the possibility of their regularization through perturbations of suitable parameters of the system. We will use the reduced coordinate given by [MATH], where [MATH] are the complex numbers representing the positions of the vortices. This choice seems very natural, although we have not come across it in the existing literature on the topic. Some of our results concerning the near-collision behavior appear to be new, and we also prove inequalities between critical energy values that we have not found in the literature. The calculations we do to analyze the collisions and near-collisions also reproduce various classical results that were previously obtained by other authors using different coordinates, and parts of the paper therefore have an expository character.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of collisions and near-collisions in the classical three-point-vortex system using Hopf fibration, symplectic reduction, and a natural reduced coordinate.
motivation: The three-vortex problem is a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, and understanding collision and near-collision behavior remains of interest in classical vortex dynamics.
method: The authors reduce the dynamics to two-dimensional symplectic leaves and introduce a reduced coordinate involving complex vortex positions to analyze collisions and their regularization.
result: They prove new inequalities between critical energy values and reproduce various classical results, with parts of the paper having an expository character.
conclusion: The work provides a natural coordinate-based approach to three-vortex collisions and near-collisions, but it lies outside quantum information theory and related research directions.

title: Structure-preserving Operator Splitting For 2.5d Ideal Mhd With An Entropy-stable Dgsem And Exactly Divergence-free Compatible Finite Elements
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a high-order, fully explicit operator-splitting method for 2.5D ideal magnetohydrodynamics on Cartesian meshes. The hydrodynamic subflow is advanced by an entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method equipped with stagewise oscillation elimination and a positivity-preserving limiter. The magnetic--velocity subflow uses compatible finite elements and mass-lumped reconstructions of electric field and current density. Its discrete-curl update exactly preserves the global [MATH] divergence-free subspace, while the ideal semidiscretization balances kinetic, magnetic, and internal energy. Curl-form artificial resistivity and a direction-resolved velocity filter return removed magnetic and kinetic energy to internal energy; consequently, the stabilized magnetic stage preserves positive internal energy and satisfies a discrete entropy inequality. The two solvers are composed by a second-order hydrodynamic--magnetic--hydrodynamic Strang splitting, yielding a matrix-free scheme that retains global mass, nodal admissibility, and magnetic divergence on accepted steps. Smooth Alfv\'en-wave and advected-vortex tests reveal an even--odd convergence pattern in the magnetic polynomial degree, verify second-order temporal accuracy, and show that stabilization preserves high-order accuracy. Field-loop, Orszag--Tang, rotor, MHD blast-wave, and Kelvin--Helmholtz calculations demonstrate robust performance for nonsmooth multidimensional flows and show that artificial resistivity suppresses grid-scale magnetic oscillations while retaining the resolved structures.
tldr: The paper develops a high-order operator-splitting scheme for 2.5D ideal magnetohydrodynamics using entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin spectral elements and divergence-free compatible finite elements.
motivation: To advance robust, high-order numerical simulation of ideal MHD flows while preserving physical invariants such as positivity, entropy stability, and divergence-free magnetic fields.
method: It composes a hydrodynamic subflow solved by an entropy-stable DGSEM with a magnetic-velocity subflow solved by compatible finite elements and curl-form artificial resistivity, coupled via second-order Strang splitting.
result: Smooth Alfvén-wave and advected-vortex tests show second-order temporal accuracy and an even-odd convergence pattern, while nonsmooth MHD benchmarks demonstrate robust performance and suppression of grid-scale magnetic oscillations.
conclusion: The scheme retains global mass, admissibility, and magnetic divergence on accepted steps, offering a matrix-free, structure-preserving approach for multidimensional ideal MHD.

title: Zonoids Whose Polars Are Zonoids: The Banach--Mazur Distance Need Not Tend To One
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every [MATH], we consider a Gaussian zonoid of revolution [MATH] arising from works of Vitale and Mathis. We prove that [MATH] is also a zonoid and compute the Banach--Mazur distance from [MATH] to the Euclidean ball. This distance is independent of the dimension and is approximately [MATH]. Consequently, the supremal Banach--Mazur distance among zonoids whose polars are zonoids does not converge to [MATH]. The construction also produces a separable real Banach space [MATH], not isometric to a Hilbert space, such that both [MATH] and [MATH] embed linearly isometrically into [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs Gaussian zonoids of revolution whose polars are also zonoids and shows that their Banach--Mazur distance to the Euclidean ball is dimension-independent, implying the supremal distance does not tend to one.
motivation: The work investigates geometric properties of zonoids and their polars in the context of Banach space theory and the Banach--Mazur distance.
method: For each dimension, the authors consider a Gaussian zonoid of revolution from Vitale and Mathis, prove that its polar is a zonoid, and compute the Banach--Mazur distance to the Euclidean ball.
result: The Banach--Mazur distance is independent of dimension and approximately a fixed value, so the supremal distance among such zonoids does not converge to one; the construction also yields a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space with certain isometric embedding properties.
conclusion: This provides a counterexample to the expectation that the Banach--Mazur distance among zonoids whose polars are zonoids tends to one, contributing to convex geometry and Banach space theory rather than quantum information.

title: The Polarity Process For The Maximum-Volume Inscribed Ellipsoid Problem
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid (MaxIE) problem for a polytope through a geometric iteration based on polarity. Given an interior point, the method forms the shifted polar polytope, computes its minimum-volume covering ellipsoid (MinCE), and then polarizes this covering ellipsoid back to obtain a new inscribed ellipsoid. This procedure was suggested by Khachiyan and Todd in 1993. Prior work studied basic polarity identities and gave an asymptotic-convergence argument for the exact process, but did not furnish a volume-ratio rate.
