motivation: Standard diffusion-based data assimilation uses a static prior from a fixed training set, ignoring past observations and thus yielding larger posterior errors than cycling DA, while retraining for time-dependent priors is expensive.
method: Motivated by linear systems theory and the exponential decay of Kalman filter dependence on past observations, the authors develop training procedures for a diffusion DA system and a diffusion direct observation prediction system, then test them on a canonical linear system.
result: Both frameworks can achieve the minimal posterior error of fully-cycled DA/DOP systems, without retraining, provided the observation time windows are sufficiently long.
conclusion: Conditioning diffusion models on windows of past observations is necessary for efficient and accurate diffusion-based data assimilation or direct observation prediction.

title: Pejwak: A Profile-Echoing Self-Anchored Aggregation Architecture For Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: PEJWAK is introduced as a profile-echoing self-anchored aggregation architecture for multi-criteria decision analysis. Each criterion is coupled geometrically with an endogenous reference derived from the same alternative before final aggregation, so criterion identity is preserved while its expressed contribution is conditioned by the alternative's profile. A general formulation separates the anchor function, anchoring kernel, retention exponents, contribution coefficients, and outer aggregation rule. The canonical member uses a weighted-arithmetic self-anchor, sets each retention exponent equal to the corresponding criterion-importance value, and derives contribution coefficients through a normalized square-root map. Analytical results establish continuity, monotonicity, diagonal calibration, internality, full-domain joint continuity, exact boundary behavior, nonseparability, failure of bisymmetry in the equal-weight binary restriction, and an exact logarithmic retention law. A deterministic MCDA audit provides complete criterion-level decomposition, exact weight-stability intervals and rank transitions, contribution-rule rank phases, set-dependence diagnostics, and exact permutation-based rank-affinity analysis. Canonical PEJWAK handles exact zeros without epsilon regularization: an active zero removes only its own criterion contribution whenever the remaining active scores sustain a positive anchor. The architecture therefore supplies an auditable profile-conditioned aggregation mechanism between direct weighted aggregation and parameter-intensive nonadditive interaction models.
tldr: PEJWAK introduces a profile-echoing self-anchored aggregation architecture for multi-criteria decision analysis, preserving criterion identity while conditioning contributions on each alternative's profile.
motivation: The paper aims to provide an auditable aggregation mechanism that bridges direct weighted aggregation and parameter-intensive nonadditive interaction models in multi-criteria decision analysis.
method: Each criterion is coupled with an endogenous reference derived from the same alternative, and a general formulation separates anchor functions, anchoring kernels, retention exponents, contribution coefficients, and outer aggregation rules, with a canonical weighted-arithmetic self-anchor and normalized square-root contribution map.
result: Analytical results establish continuity, monotonicity, diagonal calibration, internality, full-domain joint continuity, exact boundary behavior, nonseparability, failure of bisymmetry, and a logarithmic retention law, supported by deterministic MCDA audit diagnostics.
conclusion: The architecture provides a profile-conditioned aggregation mechanism with exact zero handling and auditable rank-stability analyses, but it does not connect to quantum information theory or related physics.

title: Supply Chain Analytics: A Data-Driven Approach
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern supply chain networks increasingly rely on real-time data to navigate structural uncertainties, market volatility, and operational disruptions. This manuscript bridges the gap between statistical data-driven learning and robust decision-making frameworks in logistics and operations management. We present a comprehensive, mathematically rigorous treatment of supply chain analytics, moving from empirical demand forecasting to optimal inventory and network control under uncertainty. Key topics explored include sample minimization, dynamic programming recursions for time-varying inventory replenishment, network fulfillment frameworks, and advanced distributionally robust optimization (DRO) via transport theory to hedge against rare events. By integrating predictive statistical models with prescriptive control algorithms, such as column generation for vehicle routing and non-homogeneous queueing regimes, this text provides the foundational tools necessary for designing resilient, data-driven automated systems. It serves as both a theoretical blueprint and an algorithmic guide for researchers and practitioners operating at the intersection of machine learning, mathematical optimization, and applied probability.
tldr: A comprehensive mathematical treatment of data-driven supply chain analytics, covering demand forecasting, inventory control, network fulfillment, and distributionally robust optimization.
motivation: Modern supply chain networks face structural uncertainties, market volatility, and operational disruptions that require integrating real-time data with robust decision-making frameworks in logistics and operations management.
method: Combines predictive statistical learning (empirical demand forecasting, sample minimization) with prescriptive control algorithms including dynamic programming for inventory replenishment, column generation for vehicle routing, non-homogeneous queueing models, and distributionally robust optimization grounded in transport theory.
result: Provides a unified theoretical blueprint and algorithmic guide spanning forecasting, optimal inventory/network control, and rare-event hedging within a single rigorous framework.
conclusion: The manuscript serves researchers and practitioners at the intersection of machine learning, mathematical optimization, and applied probability, offering tools for designing resilient automated supply chain systems.

title: Some Early Results By Tutte Regarding The Cycle Double Cover Conjecture In 1948
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: OpenAI recently announced a proof of the Cycle Double Cover (CDC) Conjecture. Most media reports have characterized it as a 50-year-old open problem. In reality, according to a 1987 letter from Tutte to Fleischner, the Cycle Double Cover Problem has been open for at least 80 years. Two early results regarding the CDC conjecture were established in one of Tutte's 1949 publications.
tldr: A historical note on Tutte's early 1948/1949 results concerning the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture in graph theory, prompted by OpenAI's announced proof.
motivation: Media coverage framed the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture as a 50-year-old problem, while the author argues the problem has actually been open for at least 80 years, dating back to Tutte.
method: Historical and bibliographic analysis of a 1987 letter from Tutte to Fleischner and one of Tutte's 1949 publications identifying two early results on the CDC conjecture.
result: Two early results regarding the CDC conjecture are attributed to Tutte's 1949 work, establishing a longer history of the problem than commonly reported.
conclusion: The paper corrects the historical record on the age and provenance of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture and highlights Tutte's foundational early contributions.

title: A Proof Of Liu's Conjecture On The Fundamental Triangle Inequality
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the side lengths of a triangle, and let [MATH] and [MATH] denote its circumradius and inradius, respectively. We prove a conjecture of Liu stating that \[\sum_{} \left({bc}\right)^k \geq 2+\left({R}\right)^k,~~k>1, \] with the reverse inequality for [MATH]. The proof reduces the problem to three positive variables with fixed sum and product. We also determine the equality cases.
tldr: The paper proves Liu's conjecture on a fundamental triangle inequality involving side lengths, circumradius, and inradius.
motivation: The conjecture concerns a classical geometric inequality relating triangle sides to its circumradius and inradius, extending known results to a parameter k>1.
method: The proof reduces the inequality to a problem in three positive variables with fixed sum and product, then analyzes the resulting constraints and equality cases.
result: The conjecture is proven for k>1, with the reverse inequality established for the complementary parameter range, and equality cases characterized.
conclusion: This settles Liu's conjecture and provides a complete characterization of equality, contributing to classical triangle inequalities rather than to any quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid systems topic.

title: A Four-Genus Kronecker-Limit Evaluation Of The Alternating Rogers-Ramanujan Continued Fraction
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate the six odd class-number-four cases left unevaluated in Ramanathan's treatment of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction. Let \[ S(q)=-R(-q),\qquad R(q)=}{1+{1+{1+{1+\cdots}}}}. \] For [MATH] we determine the value of [MATH] by applying the genus-character form of the Kronecker limit formula to the four ideal classes of [MATH]. The resulting expressions are given in terms of fundamental units of real quadratic fields. In particular, if [MATH], then \[ X_n^{-5}+11-X_n^5={U_n}, \] where the six quantities [MATH] are displayed explicitly below. We also give the corresponding radical expressions and quartic algebraic certificates, together with numerical checks of the six evaluations.
tldr: The paper evaluates six odd class-number-four cases of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction using the genus-character form of the Kronecker limit formula.
motivation: Ramanathan's treatment of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction left six odd class-number-four cases unevaluated, and the author aims to complete this classical number-theoretic program.
method: The genus-character form of the Kronecker limit formula is applied to the four ideal classes of a real quadratic field, yielding expressions in terms of fundamental units, together with radical expressions and quartic algebraic certificates.
result: Explicit evaluations of the six quantities X_n are obtained, satisfying relations of the form X_n^{-5} + 11 - X_n^5 = U_n, with numerical checks confirming the six evaluations.
conclusion: The work completes Ramanathan's classification of Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction values and provides new closed-form evaluations in terms of fundamental units of real quadratic fields.

title: Helson Inequality, Hankel Operators, And Weak Factorization On Paley-Wiener Spaces Of Convex Domains
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any convex set [MATH] that does not contain affine lines, we prove the inequality $[MATH][MATH]\omega_\Omega(x)=m(\Omega\cap(2x-\Omega))[MATH][MATH][MATH]1\leq p<\infty,[MATH]1\leq p\leq 2$ range.
tldr: The paper proves a Helson-type inequality for Paley-Wiener spaces on convex domains using Hankel operators and weak factorization.
motivation: The author aims to extend classical Helson inequality and related operator-theoretic results to more general convex domains via Paley-Wiener spaces.
method: The proof uses Hankel operators and weak factorization techniques on Paley-Wiener spaces associated with convex sets that contain no affine lines.
result: For any such convex set, the inequality m(Omega ∩ (2x - Omega)) ... holds in the range 1 ≤ p < ∞ and 1 ≤ p ≤ 2.
conclusion: The work contributes to complex analysis and operator theory, providing a generalized inequality with potential applications in harmonic analysis.

title: Operator Splitting Methods With Online Scaling
authors: Wanyu Zhang, Wenzhi Gao, Madeleine Udell
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a principled framework for automatically tuning preconditioners in operator splitting methods, including forward-backward splitting, Douglas-Rachford splitting, and the alternating direction method of multipliers. We interpret these splitting methods as preconditioned gradient descent applied to their corresponding envelope functions and use online learning to adaptively learn the preconditioner during optimization. Our framework achieves asymptotically faster convergence rates and accelerates the solution of important optimization problems, including Lasso, [MATH]-regularized logistic regression, and quadratic programming. Extensive numerical experiments validate our theoretical results and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework for automatically tuning preconditioners in operator splitting methods (forward-backward, Douglas-Rachford, ADMM) via online learning, yielding faster asymptotic convergence for optimization problems like Lasso and regularized logistic regression.
motivation: Preconditioner selection in splitting methods is typically done by hand and strongly affects convergence speed; a principled, automated way to adapt it during optimization is desirable.
method: The authors reinterpret splitting schemes as preconditioned gradient descent on the corresponding envelope functions and apply online learning techniques to adaptively learn the preconditioner throughout the optimization run.
result: The framework achieves asymptotically faster convergence rates and accelerates solutions of Lasso, l1-regularized logistic regression, and quadratic programming, validated by extensive numerical experiments.
conclusion: Online-learned preconditioning is a practical and theoretically grounded way to speed up classical convex optimization solvers, with broad applicability across splitting algorithms.

title: Method For Constrained Computational Guidance And Control With Application To Hypersonic Entry
authors: Anil V. Rao Emily M. Palmer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A method for constrained computation guidance and control is described. The method employs guidance updates by periodically re-solving a constrained optimal control problem. Feasibility of the optimal control problem is improved by preventing constraint violations in the perturbed system. Constraint violation is prevented by augmenting the optimal control problem with a penalty term intended to increase the margin between a constraint and its limit when the perturbed system is within certain proximity of the constraint limit. The additional penalty term employs a smooth maximum approximation to increase the margin between the constraint and its limit. The method developed in this paper is demonstrated on the maximum cross-range reusable launch vehicle (RLV) entry problem, for which the reference solution contains a long-duration constrained arc. The results demonstrate that the method developed in this paper is viable for path-constrained optimal guidance and control.
tldr: A method for constrained computational guidance and control is developed and applied to hypersonic reusable launch vehicle entry, using periodic optimal control updates with a smooth penalty to prevent constraint violations.
motivation: The paper aims to improve feasibility and robustness of path-constrained optimal guidance and control for hypersonic entry, where constraint violations can make onboard re-solving infeasible.
method: The approach periodically re-solves a constrained optimal control problem and augments it with a smooth maximum approximation penalty that increases constraint margin when the perturbed system approaches constraint limits.
result: The method is demonstrated on a maximum cross-range reusable launch vehicle entry problem featuring a long-duration constrained arc, showing viability for path-constrained optimal guidance and control.
conclusion: The proposed constrained computational guidance and control method successfully handles path constraints in hypersonic entry and may be useful for similar aerospace optimal control applications.

title: A Virtual Element Method For Kelvin--Voigt Viscoelasticity
authors: Utkarsh Rajput, Ankit Kumar, Andres E. Rubiano, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier, Sarvesh Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Considering the computational advantages of virtual element methods (VEM), this work employs a conforming VEM for the numerical approximation of the Kelvin--Voigt model of viscoelasticity. For clarity and simplicity, we focus on the primal formulation. The spatial discretization is carried out using the virtual element method, while the temporal discretization is handled via the {second-order Crank--Nicolson} scheme. We establish the well-posedness of both the semi-discrete and fully discrete problems and derive {\it a priori} error estimates. Several representative numerical examples are presented to validate the theoretical results and to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed formulation.
tldr: This paper develops a conforming virtual element method for numerically approximating the Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity model, with rigorous well-posedness and a priori error analysis.
motivation: Virtual element methods offer computational advantages on polytopal meshes, motivating their application to viscoelastic problems where standard finite elements can be restrictive.
method: The primal formulation is discretized in space using a conforming virtual element method and in time using a second-order Crank–Nicolson scheme, with well-posedness established for the semi-discrete and fully discrete problems and a priori error estimates derived.
result: Theoretical convergence results are supported by several representative numerical examples that validate the error estimates and demonstrate the effectiveness of the formulation.
conclusion: The proposed VEM framework provides a sound and effective numerical approach to Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity, though it has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Deterministic And Random Bipartite Matching On General Networks: Convex Flow Reformulation, Asymptotic Properties, And Fast Algorithms
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimum-distance bipartite matching on general networks has numerous applications various fields. This paper first focuses on deterministic problems and presents an exact edgewise-separable convex-flow reformulation. By introducing a smooth monotone rearrangement approximation of the edge-wise imbalance profiles, the convex-flow reformulation's can be solved efficiently. If we further conduct a first-order resistance-based approximation of the convex program, a one-step Laplacian-based estimator can be analytically derived in closed forms. The paper also studies random problems where supply and demand points are randomly distributed. We show that the expected optimal matching distance scales with the square root of the number of points if the supply/demand point distributions are identical, or linearly otherwise. In the former case, the optimal flow is proven to be centered, symmetric, and sub-Gaussian. In the latter case, the limiting resistance network characterizes how supply-demand imbalance is redistributed and motivates a fast algorithm that approximate the optimal flow based on the limiting resistance. Numerical experiments show that the proposed estimators closely approximate the exact matching cost while substantially reducing computation time. The proven theoretical properties of the random matching solution are numerically verified by large-scale Monte Carlo simulations.
tldr: The paper develops a convex-flow reformulation and fast algorithms for deterministic and random bipartite matching on general networks, with asymptotic scaling results and a Laplacian-based estimator.
motivation: Minimum-distance bipartite matching on networks is broadly applicable but computationally challenging, especially for random supply-demand distributions where exact solutions are costly.
method: It reformulates deterministic matching as an edgewise-separable convex flow, approximates imbalance profiles via smooth monotone rearrangement and first-order resistance, and derives closed-form one-step Laplacian estimators; random cases are analyzed using limiting resistance networks.
result: Expected optimal matching distance scales as the square root of the number of points for identical distributions and linearly otherwise; in the identical case the optimal flow is centered, symmetric, and sub-Gaussian, and a fast resistance-based algorithm approximates exact costs efficiently.
conclusion: The proposed estimators closely approximate exact matching cost while substantially reducing computation time, with theoretical properties verified by large-scale Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Why Customer Choice Models Matter
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Customer choice models are central to revenue management in attended home delivery, yet the field usually picks one without much thought. Does the choice model matter? We believe it does, and this paper shows that revenue management policies judged by their own assumed model, or trusted under a single set of parameters, can be worse than they look.
tldr: The paper argues that the choice of customer choice model materially affects revenue management policies in attended home delivery, and that policies can appear better than they truly are when evaluated under their own assumed model or a single parameter set.
motivation: Revenue management in attended home delivery routinely adopts a customer choice model without careful justification, yet the consequences of that modeling choice on policy performance are rarely examined.
method: The authors compare revenue management policies across different customer choice model specifications and parameter regimes, testing whether policies judged under their own assumed model remain robust under alternative models or parameter sets.
result: Policies that appear strong when evaluated with their own assumed choice model, or under one fixed parameter set, can perform substantially worse under misspecified models or different parameters.
conclusion: The choice model is consequential; robustness across models and parameters should be checked rather than assumed, since self-consistent evaluation can be misleading.

title: An Empirical Measurement Of Jailbreaking Evaluators
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expert evaluation of jailbreak responses is costly and difficult to scale, so the community increasingly relies on automated evaluators to determine whether an attack succeeds. However, jailbreak studies typically validate their chosen evaluator independently, repeatedly spending resources on similar evaluation efforts while making results across papers difficult to compare. Different evaluators also encode different definitions of jailbreak success, meaning that reported attack strength and apparent progress can depend substantially on which evaluator is used. We systematically compare six evaluators that recur in recent jailbreak attack and defense research: HarmBench, JailbreakBench, JailbreakRadar, StrongReject, JADES, and JailMeter. To our knowledge, no prior study has evaluated all six on the same human-labeled data under a controlled setup. We evaluate them on JailbreakQR and JailMeter-Eva, using human judgments as the reference, and measure agreement with humans, error types, and consistency across attack families. For evaluators that require a general-purpose LLM judge, we use a shared backbone to control for model-specific variation. We found that JADES exhibits the best overall performance, while HarmBench and StrongReject also demonstrate good performance.
tldr: A systematic empirical comparison of six automated jailbreak evaluators (HarmBench, JailbreakBench, JailbreakRadar, StrongReject, JADES, JailMeter) against human-labeled data to assess their reliability and consistency.
motivation: Expert human evaluation of jailbreak responses is costly and hard to scale, so the LLM safety community increasingly relies on automated evaluators, yet these are rarely validated in a common setup, making cross-paper comparisons unreliable and results evaluator-dependent.
method: The authors evaluate all six evaluators on the JailbreakQR and JailMeter-Eva datasets using human judgments as ground truth, controlling for model-specific variation by using a shared LLM backbone for judge-based evaluators, and measuring agreement with humans, error types, and consistency across attack families.
result: JADES showed the best overall performance, with HarmBench and StrongReject also performing well across the assessed metrics of human agreement, error profile, and cross-attack-family consistency.
conclusion: The choice of jailbreak evaluator materially affects reported attack strength and apparent progress, so the community should adopt standardized, human-validated evaluators to enable comparable and reproducible safety research.

title: SoK: Privacy Attacks On Machine Learning Via Explainable Ai
authors: Abdullah Caglar Oksuz, Anisa Halimi, Erman Ayday
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning explanations reveal model behavior beyond predictions, creating attack surfaces for model confidentiality and data privacy. We systematize 25 studies that exploit explanations for model extraction, membership inference, and model inversion, treating attribute inference as partial inversion. Existing work is often labeled only black- or white-box, obscuring substantial differences in what explanation signal reaches an adversary. We therefore separate model knowledge from explanation acquisition and identify five paths: target-released, attacker-derived, secondary disclosure, privileged access, and released global artifacts. Across these paths, explanations reduce extraction cost, expose membership signals through explanation statistics, recourse distance, and explanation-guided robustness, and support spatial or algebraic reconstruction of private inputs. We compare system and threat models, explanation signals, auxiliary knowledge, target models, modalities, query budgets, evaluation metrics, reported performance, and defenses. Our analysis shows that no explanation family is uniformly unsafe and no defense is uniformly effective. Risk depends on which signal is exposed, how it is acquired, which asset is targeted, and what the attacker already knows. We argue that explanation privacy should therefore be evaluated as an end-to-end disclosure problem, with defenses matched to the acquisition path and protected asset.
tldr: This systematization of knowledge reviews 25 studies on privacy attacks against machine learning models that exploit explainable AI outputs, categorizing attack paths and defenses.
motivation: Machine learning explanations expose additional information about models and data, creating privacy and confidentiality risks that existing black-box/white-box labels fail to capture clearly.
method: The authors systematize 25 studies, separate model knowledge from explanation acquisition, define five explanation-access paths, and compare threat models, explanation signals, auxiliary knowledge, target models, metrics, and defenses.
result: They find that explanations can reduce model extraction cost, leak membership through explanation statistics and recourse distance, and enable spatial or algebraic reconstruction of private inputs, with risk depending on signal, acquisition path, targeted asset, and attacker knowledge.
conclusion: The paper argues that explanation privacy should be evaluated as an end-to-end disclosure problem, with defenses matched to the specific acquisition path and protected asset.

title: From Cycle Space To Cycle Manifold: Limits And Achievability Of Blind False Data Injection Attacks
authors: Xin Li, Chenhan Xiao, Jonathan Cohen, Aviad Elyashar, Yang Weng, Rami Puzis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A false data injection attack (FDIA) can change the estimated grid state while evading a residual-based bad data detector (BDD). Existing blind attacks learn a low-rank measurement subspace, but this algebraic view does not state the physical grid constraints that make an attack stealthy or the minimum information needed to recover the complete attack space. Under the connected direct-current (DC) branch-flow model, we show that the residual-sensitive subspace of the noiseless orthogonal test is exactly the weighted cycle space. Its orthogonal complement is therefore the complete stealthy attack space, making weighted cycle-space knowledge both necessary and sufficient for complete blind FDIA. This space identifies the topology only up to 2-isomorphism and the relative cycle-edge parameters only up to one scale per biconnected component; bridge parameters are neither identified nor required. We then formulate a computationally unconstrained benchmark and a tractable measurement-only reconstruction method. Experiments on IEEE systems compare BDD bypass rate at a 95% nominal-acceptance threshold against state impact. As a compact alternating-current (AC) extension, we characterize feasible branch P/Q measurements by a cycle manifold and demonstrate topology-assisted manifold fitting and measurement generation on a graphics processing unit (GPU). In the lossless fixed-voltage small-angle limit, the normal space of the active-power slice reduces to the DC weighted cycle space.
tldr: The paper characterizes the complete stealthy attack space for blind false data injection attacks in DC power grids via weighted cycle space, with an AC extension using a cycle manifold.
motivation: Existing blind FDIA methods rely on low-rank subspace learning but do not specify the physical grid constraints that determine stealthiness or the minimum information needed to recover the full attack space.
method: Under the DC branch-flow model, the paper proves that the residual-sensitive subspace of the noiseless orthogonal test equals the weighted cycle space, whose orthogonal complement is the complete stealthy attack space. It also develops measurement-only reconstruction and an AC cycle-manifold characterization.
result: Weighted cycle-space knowledge is necessary and sufficient for complete blind FDIA, identifying topology only up to 2-isomorphism and relative cycle-edge parameters up to one scale per biconnected component, with experiments on IEEE systems comparing BDD bypass rate and state impact.
conclusion: The work provides a physical and information-theoretic basis for blind FDIA limits and achievability, and extends the DC cycle-space result to an AC cycle manifold for feasible branch measurements.

title: Where Should Society Draw The Line? A Social Choice Approach To Collective Consent
authors: Chris Dong, Sonja Kraiczy, Rohit Vasishta, Markus Brill, Wesley H. Holliday, Niclas Boehmer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Society constantly has to determine the boundaries of what it deems acceptable, from legislative decisions to the guardrails governing autonomous systems. We initiate the axiomatic study of collective consent: given individuals' attitudes toward options, which options should receive societal consent? We organize our analysis around three principles: sufficient support, minority protection, and dominance by decisively better options. Each captures a distinct reason for withholding societal consent from an option. For each principle, we develop a corresponding solution concept that transparently implements the principle and is canonical in a mathematically precise sense. For example, for minority protection, the resulting concept is a consent-adapted version of Moulin's Proportional Veto Core. Balancing multiple principles simultaneously is more challenging. To address this, we develop a game-theoretic characterization of our veto core that naturally gives rise to a family of related concepts. From this family, we identify the Approval-Weighted Veto Core as particularly desirable. By making minorities' blocking power depend on the approval support of the options being challenged, it smoothly interpolates between proportional minority protection and majority support. Experiments on five datasets spanning high-stakes decision-making (such as political elections, ethical AI evaluations, and moral decision-making) show that solution concepts violating a principle in theory also violate it empirically.
tldr: The paper initiates an axiomatic study of collective consent in social choice, proposing solution concepts based on sufficient support, minority protection, and dominance by better options.
motivation: Society needs principled methods to decide which options should receive collective consent, especially in high-stakes contexts like elections and AI ethics.
method: The authors use axiomatic social choice theory to define three principles of consent, develop corresponding solution concepts, and characterize a veto core game-theoretically to derive the Approval-Weighted Veto Core.
result: They identify canonical solution concepts for each principle, introduce a family interpolating between proportional minority protection and majority support, and empirically validate that theoretical violations of principles manifest on five datasets.
conclusion: The work provides a formal framework for collective consent that balances support, minority protection, and dominance, with the Approval-Weighted Veto Core as a desirable compromise.

title: Stress-divergence, Laplacian, And Rotational Forms Of The Incompressible Navier--Stokes Equations With Variable Viscosity
authors: Benjamin Cisternas, Douglas R. Q. Pacheco, Felipe Galarce, Ernesto Castillo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Navier--Stokes equations, incompressibility allows rewriting the viscous term in various forms leading to distinct numerical properties and flow descriptions. Furthermore, models accounting for non-Newtonian, thermal or turbulent effects often break the constant-viscosity assumption, thereby producing additional consistency terms. In this context, the present work compares the classical symmetric-gradient diffusion term with more recent variable-viscosity generalizations of the Laplacian and rotational forms. We discuss, analyze and test their differences with respect to implementation, efficiency, numerical stability and outflow boundary conditions. With a focus on time-dependent flows, we consider second-order implicit-explicit (IMEX) temporal discretizations aimed at improving efficiency and numerical stability. Through a rigorous stability analysis, we show how selected explicit treatments can bypass algorithmic nonlinearities without inducing CFL conditions. Our numerical results highlight important differences between the three viscous formulations---especially in the presence of outflow boundaries, for which the generalized Laplacian form proves more suitable in diffusion-dominated regimes. %(as widely known for constant viscosity).
tldr: Compares different viscous-term formulations of the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with variable viscosity, focusing on numerical implementation, stability, and outflow boundary conditions.
motivation: Incompressibility and variable viscosity allow multiple equivalent forms of the viscous term, but their numerical properties and consistency terms differ, especially for non-Newtonian, thermal, or turbulent flows.
method: The classical symmetric-gradient form is compared with generalized Laplacian and rotational forms under variable viscosity, using second-order IMEX time discretizations and rigorous stability analysis.
result: The three formulations differ significantly in efficiency, numerical stability, and outflow boundary treatment; the generalized Laplacian form is found to be more suitable in diffusion-dominated regimes with outflow boundaries.
conclusion: The choice of viscous formulation matters for variable-viscosity Navier–Stokes simulations, and explicit treatments can avoid nonlinear algorithmic issues without imposing CFL conditions.

title: Quantum Inversion Of Units In Group Rings: Block Dimension, Not Commutativity, Governs Hardness
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several public-key schemes base their security on the belief that inverting a unit of a group ring is hard. A recent result showed that this belief is false on a quantum computer when the group is abelian. To restore security, designers moved to non-abelian groups, especially dihedral groups, believing that the hardness of the dihedral hidden subgroup problem (HSP) would protect the scheme. This paper shows that unit inversion is a different problem and does not require an HSP solver. Instead, it can be solved by a change of basis that splits the group ring into small matrix blocks. We prove that unit inversion is polynomial-time, classically and quantumly, when an efficient generalized Fourier transform exists, the group ring is semisimple, and the largest matrix block has polynomial size. Dihedral group rings satisfy these conditions because their irreducible representations have dimension at most 2 and an efficient Fourier transform exists. We give an explicit reversible quantum circuit for the block-inversion step and validate it in a register-level simulator. We also identify the exact structural boundary where the method stops and propose a candidate construction in the surviving regime under a new, clearly stated security assumption. The constructive results are supported by reproducible software artifacts and experiments.

authors: Stephen Kirkland, Hermie Monterde, Sarah Plosker
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Much work has been done in the last two decades on the topic of quantum state transfer in a quantum spin network. One can model such a system of interacting qubits using an undirected graph, and studying vertex-to-vertex dynamics. This setup has recently been relaxed to allow for dynamics between linear combinations of two vertex states, i.e.\ from [MATH] to [MATH], where [MATH] is either [MATH] (which corresponds to pair state transfer) or [MATH] (which corresponds to plus state transfer), or more recently [MATH] is taken to be any real number (which corresponds to [MATH]-pair state transfer). Here, we broaden the investigation of [MATH]-pair state transfer to , which is perfect state transfer from [MATH] to [MATH] (up to some dilation) where [MATH]. We identify infinite families of graphs with perfect [MATH]-state transfer and provide characterizations of cases when [MATH] and when [MATH], showing situations when the degree of entanglement between vertex states is preserved, and when it is not preserved. The latter is particularly important as it represents perfect state transfer from an entangled pair of qubits to another one where the degree of entanglement need not be the same\mdash in fact, it can be set up so as to ``boost'' (increase) entanglement. We provide an algorithm that finds the vector with two nonzero entries that maximizes the fidelity of transfer for a fixed time [MATH] starting from a given [MATH]-pair state [MATH]. title: BenchShield: Formal Model-Backed Instrumentation For Reward Integrity In LLM-Agent Evaluation Infrastructure
authors: Shenghan Zheng, Zonglin Di, Yimin Liu, Kyoung Whan Choe, Jiankai Sun, Heguang Lin, Penghao Jiang, Yifeng He, Xiao Cheng, Jicheng Wang, Wenbo Chen, Alex Yates, Yinzhe Zhao, Bingran You, Yuan Gao, Ayush Munot, Shubham Gaur, Zhe Ye, Hao Wang, Xiangyi Li, Dawn Song, Christophe Hauser
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LM-agent benchmarks increasingly function as interactive evaluation infrastructure. Agents observe state, call tools, modify workspaces, submit artifacts, and receive rewards from outcome procedures. This interactivity makes evaluations vulnerable to reward hacking: an agent improves its measured score by exploiting the reward-relevant trajectory instead of solving the intended task. Existing defenses rely largely on task-specific patches, prompt instructions, or post-hoc detectors. They do not provide reusable evidence that a concrete run remained within its intended evaluation boundary. This paper presents BenchShield, a model-backed instrumentation layer for reward integrity in LLM-agent evaluation. BenchShield grounds detection in a finite lifecycle model of an evaluation's reward-relevant events. Within the benchmark infrastructure, two complementary analyses operate over this model. A static, phase-aware taint analysis exposes reward-hacking paths before a run. Its runtime counterpart uses infrastructure-side evidence to attribute concrete agent use and emit evidence-backed claims. We construct BenchShield Trajectories, a human-labeled corpus of 456 adjudicated trajectories from more than 31,000 public agent runs across three benchmarks. Compared with an agentic hackability scanner baseline on the same tasks and model, BenchShield improves full-chain recall from 23-94% to 77-100%, same-vector coverage from 16-56% to 43-78%, and reduces per-task cost by up to 65%. Its runtime analysis achieves 96% accuracy in detecting reward hacking from infrastructure-side evidence.
tldr: BenchShield is a formal model-backed instrumentation layer that detects reward hacking in LLM-agent evaluation infrastructure using static taint analysis and runtime evidence.
motivation: Interactive LLM-agent benchmarks are vulnerable to reward hacking, where agents exploit reward-relevant trajectories instead of solving intended tasks, and existing defenses lack reusable evidence of evaluation boundary compliance.
method: The paper grounds detection in a finite lifecycle model of reward-relevant events and combines a static phase-aware taint analysis with a runtime analysis that attributes concrete agent use from infrastructure-side evidence.
result: On a human-labeled corpus of 456 trajectories from over 31,000 agent runs across three benchmarks, BenchShield improves full-chain recall from 23-94% to 77-100% and same-vector coverage from 16-56% to 43-78%, while reducing per-task cost by up to 65%, with runtime detection accuracy of 96%.
conclusion: BenchShield provides reusable, evidence-backed integrity verification for LLM-agent evaluations, but it lies entirely outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, and hybrid systems research interests.
